definition_zh: 借入；借贷；借款额；借词；借用
definition_en: the act of taking money or an object on loan, the amount so taken, or a word adopted from another language
core_image: 账簿上新添的一栏，栏头写着「借入」，下面的数字一行行加长
scene: 公司财务在报表上把新借入的款项单独列成一栏，准备逐年归还。 Heavy borrowing kept the factory open through the winter.
sceneCN: 这里 borrowing 指「借入、借贷」（第 1 个义项：取得贷款这一行为）；句意为大量借贷让工厂撑过了冬天。图中可辨识物件：报表、栏线、计算器、还款计划表。

pos.zh: 借贷；借入；借款额；借词（可数或不可数）

senses.title: The act of taking a loan
senses.definition: the act of obtaining money or goods that must be repaid or returned
senses.definitionCN: 取得须偿还或归还的钱或货物的行为
senses.example: Heavy borrowing kept the factory open through the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 大量借贷让工厂撑过了冬天。
senses.why: borrow plus the noun ending -ing turns the act into a thing one can talk about, count and criticise.
senses.whyCN: borrow 加名词词尾 -ing，把动作变成可以谈论、计量与批评的事物。

senses.title: The amount borrowed
senses.definition: the total sum taken on loan, especially as shown in accounts
senses.definitionCN: 借入款项的总额，尤指账面上列示的数额
senses.example: The company's borrowings doubled in two years.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司的借款额在两年内翻了一番。
senses.why: the plural of the action noun is standard in finance for the sums owed, because each loan is a separate taking.
senses.whyCN: 金融语境中常用这个动作名词的复数指欠款总额，因为每一笔贷款都是一次单独的借入。

senses.title: A word taken from another language
senses.definition: a word adopted into one language from another, often with adapted spelling or sound
senses.definitionCN: 从另一语言吸收进某种语言的词，拼写或读音常经调整
senses.example: The dictionary lists hundreds of French borrowings.
senses.exampleCN: 这部词典列出数百个法语借词。
senses.why: linguists describe words as borrowed, so the process and the word itself both take the borrowing label.
senses.whyCN: 语言学家把词语说成借入，因此过程与词本身都带上了「借入」的标签。

senses.title: The process of linguistic borrowing
senses.definition: the historical process by which one language takes words, sounds or structures from another
senses.definitionCN: 一种语言从另一语言吸收词、语音或结构的历史过程
senses.example: Borrowing between the two languages lasted three centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 两种语言之间的借用持续了三个世纪。
senses.why: the abstract process sense lets historians talk about borrowing without naming any single word.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的过程义让史家可以谈论借用，而不必指某一个具体的词。

senses.title: A temporary player transfer
senses.definition: in sport, the arrangement by which a club takes a contracted player from another club for a period
senses.definitionCN: 体育中一家俱乐部在一定期限内取得另一家合同期内球员的安排
senses.example: The club's borrowing of the winger lasted half a season.
senses.exampleCN: 这家俱乐部租借这名边锋只持续了半个赛季。
senses.why: a player is taken temporarily and returned, so the transfer is described with the same noun as any other loan.
senses.whyCN: 球员被临时取用并归还，因此这种转会与别的借用共用同一个名词。

senses.title: An object taken for temporary use
senses.definition: a thing other than money that is taken temporarily and must be returned
senses.definitionCN: 除金钱外被临时取用、并须归还的物件
senses.example: The borrowing of the ladder saved them a trip to the shop.
senses.exampleCN: 借来这把梯子让他们省了一趟去店里的路。
senses.why: the everyday sense never died out, even though finance now dominates the word.
senses.whyCN: 尽管金融义如今占主导，这个日常义从未消失。

senses.title: Reliance on others' ideas
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：沿用他人的想法
senses.definition: figuratively, the taking of ideas, styles or methods from another source without owning them
senses.definitionCN: 比喻上指从另一来源取用想法、风格或方法，却不真正拥有
senses.example: The composer's borrowing from folk songs is openly acknowledged.
senses.exampleCN: 这位作曲家对民歌的借用是公开承认的。
senses.why: ideas are treated as goods that can be taken on loan and handed back in altered form.
senses.whyCN: 想法被当作可以借走、并以改变形式交还的货物。

senses.title: Public-sector borrowing
senses.definition: the amount a government or public body must raise in a year to cover the gap between spending and revenue
senses.definitionCN: 政府或公共机构为弥补收支缺口而在一年内必须筹措的金额
senses.example: Public borrowing rose as tax receipts fell.
senses.exampleCN: 税收下降之际，公共部门举债上升。
senses.why: the aggregate sense treats all the state's loans as one measurable flow with economic effects.
senses.whyCN: 总量义把国家的所有借款看作一个有经济影响的可测流量。

intro.en: Borrowing is the native verb borrow plus the noun ending -ing; borrow itself goes back to Old English borgian and has no Latin source. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: borrowing 是本族动词 borrow 加名词词尾 -ing；borrow 本身可追溯到古英语 borgian，没有拉丁来源。年代均为约数。

items.en: Borgian meant 'to borrow' and also 'to lend'; the verb described a transaction secured by a pledge rather than a one-way transfer.
items.cn: borgian 既指「借入」也指「借出」；这个动词描述的是以抵押作保的交易，而非单向转移。

items.en: The noun borg 'pledge, surety' supplied the security behind the deal, and the verb was formed on it.
items.cn: 名词 borg「抵押、担保」提供交易背后的保障，动词即由此构成。

items.en: Cognates include Old Norse borga and German borgen, all built on lending against a pledge.
items.cn: 同源词包括古诺斯语 borga 与德语 borgen，都建立在凭抵押借贷之上。

items.en: The ending -ing is the native English suffix for an activity or its result, so borrowing names the act and, in the plural, the sums taken.
items.cn: 词尾 -ing 是英语本族表示活动或其结果的后缀，因此 borrowing 指行为，复数则指借入的款项。

items.en: From the nineteenth century linguists used borrowing for words taken from other languages, extending the money metaphor to vocabulary.
items.cn: 从 19 世纪起，语言学家用 borrowing 指从其他语言吸收的词，把金钱比喻扩展到词汇。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the first use of the financial plural is not precisely dated, and the pre-Germanic origin of borg is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：金融复数的最早用例没有确切年代，borg 在日耳曼语之前的来源属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same stem or with a similar shape; group two holds financial aggregates that overlap with borrowing in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干或字形相近的形式；第二组是在含义上与 borrowing 重叠的金融总量词。

entries.definition: The act of taking on loan; borrowing is the same act turned into a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 借入的动作；borrowing 是同一动作变成名词。

entries.definition: The person who borrows; the ending -er marks a person, while -ing marks the act.
entries.definitionCN: 借入的人；-er 标记人，-ing 标记行为。

entries.definition: The act of giving on loan; borrowing and lending are the two sides of one transaction.
entries.definitionCN: 出借的行为；借入与出借是同一笔交易的两面。

entries.definition: The plural is a finance term for total debt, not merely several acts of borrowing.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式是金融术语，指债务总额，不只是多次借入行为。

entries.definition: The obligation left after borrowing; borrowing is the flow, debt is the stock.
entries.definitionCN: 借入之后留下的偿付义务；borrowing 是流量，debt 是存量。

entries.definition: A single sum lent; borrowing can cover many loans and need not be arranged with a bank.
entries.definitionCN: 单笔借出的款项；borrowing 可涵盖多笔贷款，且未必经由银行。

entries.definition: Borrowed money used to amplify returns; it stresses the investment strategy, not the act of borrowing.
entries.definitionCN: 用来放大收益的借入资金；强调投资策略，而非借入行为。

entries.definition: Money that is late, not money newly borrowed; it marks a failure to pay on time.
entries.definitionCN: 逾期未付的钱，不是新借入的钱；它标记未能按时付款。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: borrow + -ing: the act of taking on loan, and in the plural the sums taken.
normal.cn: borrow 加 -ing：借入的行为，复数则指借入的款项。

normal.en: The family runs borrow, borrower, borrowing, borrowings and borrowable.
normal.cn: 同族包括 borrow、borrower、borrowing、borrowings 与 borrowable。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: government borrowing, heavy borrowing, corporate borrowing, foreign borrowing.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：政府举债、大量借贷、企业借款、对外借款。

normal.en: Borrow and lend are the two directions of one deal.
normal.cn: 借入与借出是一笔交易的两个方向。

normal.en: Borrowing is also the word linguists use for words taken from other languages.
normal.cn: borrowing 也是语言学家用来指从其他语言吸收词语的词。

abstract.en: Picture a column of figures that grows longer every month.
abstract.cn: 想象一列数字每个月都变得更长。

abstract.en: Picture a word moving house into a new language and keeping its old furniture.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词搬进新语言，还带着旧家具。

abstract.en: Picture a player wearing another club's shirt for half a season.
abstract.cn: 想象一名球员穿着另一家俱乐部的球衣半个赛季。

examples.en: Borrowing is cheaper when interest rates are low.
examples.cn: 利率低时借贷更便宜。

examples.en: The government cut borrowing after the recovery.
examples.cn: 经济复苏后政府削减了举债。

examples.en: The word comes from a borrowing made in the sixteenth century.
examples.cn: 这个词来自 16 世纪的一次借用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「borrow（借入）+ ing（行为）」——借进来的这件事或这笔钱 → 借贷、借款额

root: 古英语 borgian「借入（亦曾指借出）」+ 本族名词词尾 -ing；borgian 与 borg「抵押、担保」相关。无拉丁来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act: taking something on loan, and the same noun covers the act, the sum, a word taken into a language, a transferred player and a public deficit.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把某物借入，同一个名词涵盖行为、金额、被语言吸收的词、被租借的球员以及公共赤字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a new column headed 'taken on loan' with figures growing down the page.
core.cn: 核心意象：报表上新添一栏，栏头写着「借入」，数字沿页面往下增长。

branches.en: THE ACT ITSELF: money or a ladder, the taking is the same and must be undone.
branches.cn: 行为本身：无论是钱还是梯子，取用都一样，且都须归还。

branches.en: THE STOCK: the plural turns many takings into one figure of debt.
branches.cn: 存量：复数把多次借入变成一个债务数字。

branches.en: WORDS TAKEN: one borrowed word and the whole historical process share the label.
branches.cn: 借来的词：单个借词与整个历史过程共用这个标签。

branches.en: PLAYERS TAKEN: a club borrows a contracted player and returns him.
branches.cn: 借来的球员：俱乐部借入合同期内的球员，再归还。

branches.en: IDEAS AND DEFICITS: composers borrow styles, and states borrow to cover spending.
branches.cn: 想法与赤字：作曲家借用风格，国家借钱弥补开支。

intro.en: Borrowing is a native stem plus a native noun ending, so its parts are English and its meaning is the act or the result of taking on loan.
intro.cn: borrowing 是一个本族词干加本族名词词尾，两个部分都属英语，含义是借入这一动作或其结果。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source; the Latin words for a loan and for borrowing belong to other roots and are not ancestors of this form.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁来源；拉丁语表示贷款与借入的词属于别的词根，并不是这一形式的祖先。

items.meaning: to take with a promise to return
items.example: They borrow the boat every summer.
items.exampleCN: 他们每年夏天都借这条船。

items.structure: Old English -ing (noun of action or result)
items.example: The ending turns the verb into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动词变成名词。

items.meaning: the act of taking on loan
items.example: Borrowing funded the new line.
items.exampleCN: 借贷为这条新生产线提供了资金。

items.example: Borrowings appear on the balance sheet.
items.exampleCN: 借款额列在资产负债表上。

items.example: The borrower repaid in full.
items.exampleCN: 借款人全额偿还。

items.example: The borrowed tune became a hit.
items.exampleCN: 这首借来的曲子成了热门。

items.example: Only borrowable items leave the desk.
items.exampleCN: 只有可外借的物品才离开服务台。

items.meaning: the act of giving on loan
items.example: Lending and borrowing must balance.
items.exampleCN: 出借与借入必须平衡。

definition_zh: 乘法；成倍增加；增殖；繁殖；乘法运算
definition_en: the arithmetic operation of adding a number to itself a given number of times, or a large increase in number
core_image: 同样的几堆积木一排排摆开，堆数与每堆的块数交错相乘
scene: 课桌上摆开三排同样多的积木，孩子一排排数。 The teacher introduces multiplication as repeated addition of equal groups.
sceneCN: 这里 multiplication 指「把若干相同数量的组相加的运算」（第 1 个义项：算术乘法）；句意为老师把乘法讲成相同组的重复相加。图中可辨识物件：积木、三排、课桌、孩子的手。

pos.zh: 乘法；增殖；繁殖；成倍增加

senses.title: The arithmetic operation
senses.definition: the operation of combining equal groups, or of adding a number to itself repeatedly
senses.definitionCN: 把若干相同数量的组合起来的运算，或把一个数重复相加
senses.example: The teacher introduces multiplication as repeated addition of equal groups.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把乘法讲成相同组的重复相加。
senses.why: multiplication is a folding of many equal copies into one total, which is exactly what the Latin root says.
senses.whyCN: 乘法就是把许多相同的副本叠合成一个总数，这正是拉丁词根说的意思。

senses.title: A large increase in number
senses.definition: a rapid or repeated increase in the number of something
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的数量迅速或反复地增加
senses.example: The multiplication of small shops changed the old market street.
senses.exampleCN: 小店铺的成倍增加改变了那条老市场街。
senses.why: the arithmetic operation reuses the same image outside arithmetic: many copies of one thing appear at once.
senses.whyCN: 算术运算把同一个形象用到算外：同一件东西一下子冒出许多副本。

senses.title: Cell multiplication
senses.definition: the process by which cells divide and increase in number
senses.definitionCN: 细胞分裂、数量增多的过程
senses.example: Uncontrolled cell multiplication is the mark of a tumour.
senses.exampleCN: 不受控制的细胞增殖是肿瘤的标志。
senses.why: biology describes tissues growing by copies, and the arithmetic word for copying fits the process exactly.
senses.whyCN: 生物学描述组织靠副本增长，而算术里表示「复制叠加」的词正合这个过程。

senses.title: Reproduction of animals
senses.definition: the increase of a population by breeding
senses.definitionCN: 种群通过繁育而数量增多
senses.example: The multiplication of the herd surprised the ranchers.
senses.exampleCN: 牛群的繁殖速度让牧场主吃惊。
senses.why: when animals breed, their numbers fold upward, so the older word for increase became a word for breeding.
senses.whyCN: 动物繁育时数量层层上翻，于是那个表示「增多」的老词成了繁育的词。

senses.title: The multiplication table
senses.definition: a printed grid of products of small numbers used for learning
senses.definitionCN: 印成网格、供学习使用的小数目乘积表
senses.example: She recited the multiplication table from memory.
senses.exampleCN: 她凭记忆背出了乘法表。
senses.why: the table is the operation written out in full, so it carries the name of the operation itself.
senses.whyCN: 乘法表就是把运算全部写出来，因此它带着运算本身的名字。

senses.title: Matrix multiplication
senses.definition: the rule for combining two arrays of numbers by summing products of rows and columns
senses.definitionCN: 把两个数字阵列按行与列的乘积求和来合并的规则
senses.example: Matrix multiplication is not commutative, so order matters.
senses.exampleCN: 矩阵乘法不满足交换律，所以顺序要紧。
senses.why: the operation sums products, which is a generalized multiplication of many terms at once.
senses.whyCN: 这个运算把许多乘积加起来，等于一次对许多项做推广的乘法。

senses.title: The multiplication sign
senses.definition: the symbol placed between numbers to show that they are multiplied
senses.definitionCN: 写在两个数之间、表示相乘的符号
senses.example: The multiplication sign was changed to a dot in the printed formula.
senses.exampleCN: 在印刷的公式里，乘号被改成了一个小点。
senses.why: the written sign is the operation made visible, so it is named after the operation.
senses.whyCN: 这个书写符号是运算的可见形式，因此以运算命名。

senses.title: The combined effect of several causes
senses.definition: the way separate efforts or causes reinforce one another
senses.definitionCN: 各自分开的努力或原因相互增强的方式
senses.example: The multiplication of small savings made the plan affordable.
senses.exampleCN: 一笔笔小节省叠加起来，让这个计划负担得起。
senses.why: effects that reinforce one another combine like equal groups, so the word for multiplying serves as a metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 相互增强的效果像相同的组一样合并，于是「相乘」这个词成了比喻。

senses.title: Logical multiplication
senses.definition: the Boolean operation that gives true only when every input is true
senses.definitionCN: 只有当所有输入都为真时才给出真的布尔运算
senses.example: Logical multiplication corresponds to the word and.
senses.exampleCN: 逻辑乘法对应的是「与」这个词。
senses.why: Boolean algebra borrows the arithmetic name because true and false combine in a strict table, like factors in a product.
senses.whyCN: 布尔代数借用算术名称，因为真假按严格的表组合，像乘积里的因子。

intro.en: Multiplication is Latin multiplicatio 'a multiplying', from multiplicare, built on multiplex 'many-fold', itself multus 'many' plus -plex 'fold'. English took it through French.
intro.cn: multiplication 是拉丁 multiplicatio「使增多」，出自 multiplicare，而后者建立在 multiplex「多重的」上，即 multus「多」加 -plex「折叠」。英语经法语引入。

items.en: Multus meant 'many, much'. It supplies the first half of the word and also appears in multiple and multitude.
items.cn: multus 意为「多」。它提供这个词的前半部分，也出现在 multiple 与 multitude 里。

items.en: Plicare meant 'to fold'. The same verb gives complicate, explicit, duplicate and multiply, all images of folding layers together.
items.cn: plicare 意为「折叠」。同一个动词给出 complicate、explicit、duplicate 与 multiply，都是把层叠起来的形象。

items.en: Multus plus -plex produced multiplex 'many-fold, manifold', the adjective behind the whole family.
items.cn: multus 加 -plex 产生 multiplex「多重的、层叠的」，这是整个词族背后的形容词。

items.en: The verb multiplicare meant 'to make many-fold, to increase', and arithmetic narrowed it to the operation of repeated addition.
items.cn: 动词 multiplicare 意为「使成多重、使增多」，算术把它收窄为重复相加的运算。

items.en: Old French multiplication brought the noun into English in the fourteenth century, first in arithmetic and later in biology.
items.cn: 古法语 multiplication 在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，先用于算术，后来用于生物学。

items.en: The first English date for the biological sense is approximate; the Latin pieces and the arithmetic sense are well documented.
items.cn: 生物学义的最早英语年代为约数；拉丁构件与算术义则有充分文献记录。

note.en: The first group shares the folding root and is easily confused; the second group names growth and reproduction.
note.cn: 第一组共享那个表示「折叠」的词根，容易混淆；第二组是增长与繁殖的说法。

entries.definition: The verb of the operation; multiplication is the noun naming the act or the result.
entries.definitionCN: 运算的动词；multiplication 则是命名动作或结果的名词。

entries.definition: A number that another number divides exactly, or an adjective meaning many; it is not the operation.
entries.definitionCN: 指能被另一个数整除的数，或形容词「多个的」；不是运算本身。

entries.definition: The quality of being many; it counts kinds or instances, not products.
entries.definitionCN: 指「多」的性质；数的是种类或实例，不是乘积。

entries.definition: From explicare 'to unfold'; it means fully stated, and shares plicare without any arithmetic sense.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 explicare「展开」；意为明确说出的，共享 plicare 但没有算术义。

entries.definition: From duo plus plicare, 'folded twice'; it means an exact copy, not a multiplication.
entries.definitionCN: 由 duo 加 plicare 构成，意为「折两次」；指完全相同的副本，不是乘法。

entries.definition: Any growth in size or number; multiplication suggests growth by copies or factors.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指大小或数量的增长；multiplication 暗示按副本或倍数增长。

entries.definition: A rapid increase in number, especially of cells or weapons; it stresses spread rather than the arithmetic rule.
entries.definitionCN: 指数量迅速增多，尤指细胞或武器；强调扩散而非算术规则。

entries.definition: The process by which living things produce offspring; multiplication can name the resulting increase.
entries.definitionCN: 指生物产生后代的过程；multiplication 可以指由此产生的数量增长。

entries.definition: Growth in size or scope; it does not imply equal groups or repeated addition.
entries.definitionCN: 指规模或范围的扩大；不含相同组或重复相加的意思。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin pieces, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁构件、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: multus 'many' plus plicare 'fold': many layers folded into one total.
normal.cn: multus「多」加 plicare「折」：许多层叠成一个总数。

normal.en: The family runs multiply, multiple, multiplicity, multiplication and multiplicative.
normal.cn: 同族词有 multiply、multiple、multiplicity、multiplication 与 multiplicative。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: multiplication table, matrix multiplication, multiplication sign.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：乘法表、矩阵乘法、乘号。

normal.en: Repeated addition of equal groups is the whole secret of the operation.
normal.cn: 相同组的重复相加，就是这项运算的全部秘密。

normal.en: Plicare also folds complicate, explicit and duplicate, so the family is all about layers.
normal.cn: plicare 还折出 complicate、explicit 与 duplicate，这个词族全都关于层叠。

abstract.en: Picture three trays, each holding four eggs, and the count arriving all at once.
abstract.cn: 想象三个托盘，每盘四个蛋，总数一下子就算出来了。

abstract.en: Picture a choir where every singer brings a friend, and the rows double.
abstract.cn: 想象合唱团里每个歌手都带来一个朋友，排数就翻倍了。

abstract.en: Picture one small saving repeated in many places until it becomes a large sum.
abstract.cn: 想象一笔小节省在许多地方重复出现，最后变成一大笔钱。

examples.en: Multiplication is commutative, so the order of the factors does not change the product.
examples.cn: 乘法满足交换律，因子的顺序不改变乘积。

examples.en: The multiplication of algae turned the pond green within a week.
examples.cn: 藻类的成倍繁殖让池塘一周内变绿。

examples.en: Matrix multiplication must be done in the stated order.
examples.cn: 矩阵乘法必须按规定的顺序进行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「满多」——相同的组越叠越多 → 乘法、成倍增加

root: 拉丁 multus「多」+ plicare「折叠」→ multiplex「多重的」→ multiplicare「使增多」→ multiplicatio → 古法语 → 英语 multiplication。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all fold equal copies together: the arithmetic operation, a manyfold rise, cells and herds, the printed table, matrices, the written sign, combined effects and a logical conjunction.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都把相同的副本叠在一起：算术运算、成倍上升、细胞与畜群、印好的表、矩阵、写下的符号、叠加的效果，以及逻辑上的合取。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: equal stacks of blocks laid in rows, counted by row times blocks.
core.cn: 核心意象：同样多的积木堆成几排，用排数乘每堆块数来数。

branches.en: THE OPERATION AND ITS TABLE: repeated addition, and the grid that writes it all out.
branches.cn: 运算与它的表：重复相加，以及把它全部写出的网格。

branches.en: MANYFOLD RISE: a rapid increase in number, and separate efforts reinforcing one another.
branches.cn: 成倍上升：数量的快速增多，以及分开的努力相互增强。

branches.en: LIFE MULTIPLYING: cells dividing and herds breeding, both growth by copies.
branches.cn: 生命在增殖：细胞分裂与畜群繁育，都是靠副本增长。

branches.en: FOLDING IN ROWS: matrix products and the written sign that marks the operation.
branches.cn: 按行折叠：矩阵的乘积，以及标记这项运算的书写符号。

branches.en: LOGICAL AND: true only when every factor is true, like a product that vanishes when any factor is zero.
branches.cn: 逻辑上的「与」：只有每个因子都真才为真，如同任何因子为零则乘积为零。

intro.en: Multiplication is a Latin action noun built from 'many' and 'fold'; both pieces and the suffix build a large family.
intro.cn: multiplication 是由「多」与「折叠」构成的拉丁动作名词；两个构件与后缀都构成一个很大的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin multus and plicare give multiple, multiplex, multiply, explicit, complicate and duplicate; the suffix -io, through French -ion, names the action or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 multus 与 plicare 衍生 multiple、multiplex、multiply、explicit、complicate 与 duplicate；后缀 -io 经法语 -ion 命名动作或结果。

items.example: The first element supplies the many.
items.exampleCN: 第一个构件提供「多」。

items.example: The second element supplies the folding.
items.exampleCN: 第二个构件提供「折叠」。

items.example: The adjective describes many layers.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述许多层。

items.example: The verb is the act of folding many together.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是把许多层叠起来的动作。

items.example: The noun names the operation.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名这项运算。

items.example: Multiply the length by the width.
items.exampleCN: 把长乘以宽。

items.meaning: a number that divides another exactly
items.example: Twelve is a multiple of three.
items.exampleCN: 十二是三的倍数。

items.example: The multiplicity of options confused them.
items.exampleCN: 选项的繁多让他们困惑。

items.example: The instructions were explicit.
items.exampleCN: 说明写得很明确。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词后缀
items.example: It turns the verb of multiplying into the name of the act.
items.exampleCN: 它把「乘」的动词变成这项动作的名称。

definition_zh: 遗产；继承的财产；世代相传的传统与文化；出身与天赋权利；历史遗迹与自然遗产
definition_en: property, traditions or culture passed down from earlier generations
core_image: 阁楼上那台旧织机蒙着布，几代人搬了几次家都没舍得丢
scene: 阁楼上那台旧织机蒙着布，几代人搬了几次家都没舍得丢， The family keeps the loom as part of its heritage.
sceneCN: 这里 heritage 指「从先辈继承下来、代代保留的财物」（第 1 个义项：继承的财产）；句意为这家人把那台织机当作遗产的一部分保留下来。图中可辨识物件：蒙布的织机、木楼梯、旧箱子、系着标签的钥匙。

pos.zh: 遗产；继承的财产；世代相传的传统与文化；历史遗迹

senses.title: Property inherited from ancestors
senses.definition: money, land or objects received from a predecessor, especially within a family
senses.definitionCN: 从前人、尤指家族成员那里接受的金钱、土地或物件
senses.example: The family keeps the loom as part of its heritage.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人把那台织机当作遗产的一部分保留下来。
senses.why: The oldest sense is legal and material: heritage is what passes to an heir when an owner dies.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是法律与物质上的：遗产是业主去世后传给继承人的东西。

senses.title: Traditions and values passed down
senses.titleCN: 世代相传的传统与价值观
senses.definition: customs, beliefs, stories and skills handed from one generation to the next
senses.definitionCN: 一代代传下的习俗、信念、故事与技艺
senses.example: The village's heritage lives in its songs more than in its buildings.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村庄的遗产更多活在歌谣里，而不是建筑里。
senses.why: The legal handover is reused for culture: what is passed down may be a way of doing things rather than a deed.
senses.whyCN: 法律上的交接被挪用到文化上：传下来的可能是做事的方式，而不是一纸契据。

senses.title: Birthright and inherited status
senses.titleCN: 与生俱来的权利与继承的身份
senses.definition: the rights, rank or identity one holds by birth or family line
senses.definitionCN: 因出生或家族世系而拥有的权利、等级或身份
senses.example: She wears the ring as a sign of her heritage, not of her wealth.
senses.exampleCN: 她戴这枚戒指，表示的是她的出身，而不是财富。
senses.why: Heritage can be intangible in a social sense: a name or a rank arrives without any object changing hands.
senses.whyCN: 遗产在社会意义上可以是无形的：一个姓氏或一个等级到手时，并没有任何物件易手。

senses.title: Built heritage
senses.definition: historic buildings, monuments and townscapes valued as a collective inheritance
senses.definitionCN: 被当作集体继承物而珍视的历史建筑、纪念物与城镇景观
senses.example: The trust lists the mill as built heritage and forbids its demolition.
senses.exampleCN: 该信托机构把磨坊列为建筑遗产，禁止拆除。
senses.why: When a whole society inherits a building, the private word becomes public and legal.
senses.whyCN: 当整个社会继承一栋建筑，这个私人词汇就变成公共与法律用语。

senses.title: Natural heritage
senses.definition: landscapes, habitats and species treated as an inheritance worth protecting
senses.definitionCN: 被当作值得保护的继承物来对待的景观、栖息地与物种
senses.example: The valley's natural heritage includes the old orchard varieties.
senses.exampleCN: 这座山谷的自然遗产包括那些古老的果树品种。
senses.why: Heritage can be extended to what no human made: a landscape is inherited too, and can be lost like a building.
senses.whyCN: 遗产可以扩展到并非人造之物：一片景观也是继承来的，也会像建筑一样失去。

senses.title: The roots that shape identity
senses.definition: the inherited culture through which a person or group understands who they are
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或群体借以理解自身身份来源的继承文化
senses.example: He returned to the old quarter to recover a heritage he had never learned.
senses.exampleCN: 他回到老城区，想找回一份自己从未学过的遗产。
senses.why: Heritage answers the question where do I come from, so it becomes a resource for identity rather than a possession.
senses.whyCN: 遗产回答「我从哪里来」，因此它成为认同的资源，而非一件所有物。

senses.title: Heritage as tourism and industry
senses.titleCN: 作为旅游与产业的遗产
senses.definition: inherited places and traditions packaged and sold as visitor attractions
senses.definitionCN: 被包装并作为游客吸引物出售的继承场所与传统
senses.example: The heritage industry restored the harbour and then raised the ticket price.
senses.exampleCN: 遗产产业修复了港口，随后提高了票价。
senses.why: A public inheritance needs money to survive, and selling access to it creates a business with its own interests.
senses.whyCN: 公共继承物需要钱才能存活，而出售接近它的权利，就造出一个有自身利益的产业。

senses.title: The legacy of a movement or era
senses.titleCN: 一场运动或一个时代的遗泽
senses.definition: the achievements or consequences that later people receive from an earlier movement or period
senses.definitionCN: 后来者从较早的运动或时期那里继承的成就或后果
senses.example: Public libraries are part of the heritage of the reform movement.
senses.exampleCN: 公共图书馆是那场改革运动的遗泽之一。
senses.why: The family image widens one last time: a generation can inherit not only from relatives but from a struggle it never joined.
senses.whyCN: 家族的意象最后一次被放宽：一代人不仅可以从亲属那里继承，也可以从一场自己未曾参与的抗争中继承。

intro.en: Heritage comes through Old French from Late Latin hereditare, to inherit, built on Latin heres, heir. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: heritage 经古法语来自晚期拉丁语 hereditare「继承」，后者由拉丁语 heres「继承人」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Heres meant heir. Its deeper origin is source uncertain, and it is not securely linked to another Latin root.
items.cn: heres 意为「继承人」。它更早的来源不确定，也没有可靠地联系到另一个拉丁词根。

items.en: Hereditare, to inherit or to leave by will, was formed on the hered- stem of heres and its noun hereditas, inheritance.
items.cn: hereditare 意为「继承或按遗嘱留下」，由 heres 的词干 hered- 及其名词 hereditas「继承」构成。

items.en: Old French eritage named an inherited estate; the h was restored in English spelling under Latin influence.
items.cn: 古法语 eritage 指继承的产业；英语拼写受拉丁语影响又补回了 h。

items.en: Middle English heritage first meant inherited property and the right to inherit it.
items.cn: 中古英语 heritage 最初指继承的财产以及继承它的权利。

items.en: From the eighteenth century the word widened from private property to the shared past of a people, and later to buildings and landscapes.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，这个词从私人财产扩展到民族共有的过去，后来又扩展到建筑与景观。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English use of the cultural sense is not securely dated, and the origin of heres remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定：文化义在英语中的最早使用没有确切年代；heres 的来源亦无定论。

note.en: The first group holds words from the heir root that differ in word class; the second holds near synonyms for what is passed down.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「继承人」词根、但词性不同的词；第二组是表示「传下之物」的近义词。

entries.definition: To receive property, traits or traditions from a predecessor; heritage is the noun for what is received.
entries.definitionCN: 从前人那里接受财产、性状或传统；heritage 是表示所接受之物的名词。

entries.definition: The property or traits received, especially in law or genetics; heritage is broader and often cultural.
entries.definitionCN: 所接受的财产或性状，尤其在法律或遗传学中；heritage 更宽，常指文化。

entries.definition: Passed from parent to child by blood or legal line; it describes the route of transmission, not the thing transmitted.
entries.definitionCN: 由血统或法定世系从父母传给子女；它描述传递路径，而非传递之物。

entries.definition: Capable of being inherited, used of property or traits; it is a technical adjective, not the noun heritage.
entries.definitionCN: 可被继承的，用于财产或性状；它是技术性形容词，不是名词 heritage。

entries.definition: Something handed down, often with a personal or historical tone; heritage is more collective and more official.
entries.definitionCN: 前人留下之物，常带个人或历史语气；heritage 更集体、更官方。

entries.definition: An inheritance from ancestors, especially national or religious property; it is more formal and more legal than heritage.
entries.definitionCN: 祖先传下的遗产，尤指国家或宗教财产；比 heritage 更正式、更法律化。

entries.definition: A custom or belief passed down by repeated practice; it is one kind of heritage, not its whole body.
entries.definitionCN: 通过反复实践传下的习俗或信念；它是遗产的一种，而非全部。

entries.definition: A right or property one holds from birth; it stresses entitlement, while heritage stresses the handover.
entries.definitionCN: 因出生而拥有的权利或财产；它强调应得资格，而 heritage 强调交接。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real heir root, the real family and the phrases the word actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「继承人」词根、真实的同族词，以及这个词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: heritage shares the hered- stem with inherit and inheritance: all point to a handover to an heir.
normal.cn: heritage 与 inherit（继承）、inheritance（继承、遗产）共享 hered- 词干：都指向把东西交给继承人。

normal.en: The family runs heritage, inherit, inheritance, hereditary, heritable and inheritor.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 heritage（遗产）、inherit（继承）、inheritance（继承、遗产）、hereditary（世袭的）、heritable（可继承的）、inheritor（继承人）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: national heritage, world heritage, heritage site, heritage industry.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：国家遗产、世界遗产、遗产地、遗产产业。

normal.en: The word moved from a private will to a public past, then to buildings and landscapes.
normal.cn: 这个词从一份私人遗嘱移到公共的过去，再移到建筑与景观。

normal.en: A useful contrast: inheritance is legal and technical, while heritage is cultural and collective.
normal.cn: 有用的对照：inheritance 是法律与技术用语，而 heritage 是文化与集体用语。

abstract.en: Picture a trunk in an attic, labelled not with a name but with a generation.
abstract.cn: 想象阁楼上的一只箱子，标签上写的不是名字，而是一代人。

abstract.en: Picture a key that opens a door its owner has never seen.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙，打开一扇它的主人从未见过的门。

abstract.en: Picture a river that carries the silt of fields no living farmer ploughed.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河，载着在世农夫从未犁过的田地的泥沙。

examples.en: The museum treats the dialect recordings as heritage rather than as data.
examples.cn: 博物馆把方言录音当作遗产，而不是数据。

examples.en: World heritage status brought money and also brought crowds.
examples.cn: 世界遗产地位带来了钱，也带来了人潮。

examples.en: Heritage is not only what survives; it is what someone chooses to hand on.
examples.cn: 遗产不只是幸存下来的东西；它是有人选择传下去的东西。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喝瑞替吉」听成「喝了记得」——先辈留下的老屋与歌谣，喝了水也要记得，就是遗产。

root: 经古法语 eritage 来自晚期拉丁语 hereditare「继承」，后者由拉丁语 heres「继承人」及其词干 hered- 构成，并与 hereditas「继承」同族。heres 的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one handover: property, traditions, status, built places, natural places, identity, tourism and finally the legacy of a movement.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次交接展开：财产、传统、身份、建筑、自然场所、认同、旅游，最后是一场运动的遗泽。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an object passed from a dying hand to a living one, with no receipt.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件东西从将逝的手交到活着的手里，没有收据。

branches.en: PRIVATE INHERITANCE: property and status pass to an heir, whether or not any object changes hands.
branches.cn: 私人继承：财产与身份传给继承人，无论是否有物件易手。

branches.en: CULTURE: songs, skills and beliefs are inherited like an estate.
branches.cn: 文化：歌谣、技艺与信念像产业一样被继承。

branches.en: BUILT: a whole society becomes the heir of a building.
branches.cn: 建筑：整个社会成为一栋建筑的继承人。

branches.en: NATURAL: landscapes are inherited too and can be lost like buildings.
branches.cn: 自然：景观也是继承来的，也会像建筑一样失去。

branches.en: IDENTITY, INDUSTRY AND MOVEMENT: heritage becomes roots, then a business, then the legacy of a struggle.
branches.cn: 认同、产业与运动：遗产先成为根，再成为生意，最后成为一场抗争的遗泽。

intro.en: Heritage is built on a Latin stem for heir, and that stem also produces inherit, inheritance and hereditary.
intro.cn: heritage 建立在表示「继承人」的拉丁词干上，这个词干还产生 inherit、inheritance 与 hereditary。

latinIntro.en: Latin heres, heir, and hereditas, inheritance, supply the hered- stem; Late Latin hereditare gives the verb that French turned into eritage.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 heres「继承人」与 hereditas「继承」提供 hered- 词干；晚期拉丁语 hereditare 给出动词，法语又把它变成 eritage。

items.example: The stem hered- runs through the whole family.
items.exampleCN: hered- 词干贯穿整个词族。

items.example: The noun named both the act and the property.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词既指继承行为，也指继承的财产。

items.meaning: to inherit; to leave by will
items.example: French hériter and English inherit both descend from it.
items.exampleCN: 法语 hériter 与英语 inherit 都由此而来。

items.example: The loom is family heritage.
items.exampleCN: 这台织机是家族遗产。

items.example: She inherited the house.
items.exampleCN: 她继承了这所房子。

items.example: The inheritance was divided among four children.
items.exampleCN: 遗产分给了四个孩子。

items.example: The office was hereditary.
items.exampleCN: 这个职位是世袭的。

items.example: The land is heritable under the old law.
items.exampleCN: 按旧法，这片土地可以继承。

items.meaning: the passing of traits from parents
items.example: Heredity explains part of the pattern.
items.exampleCN: 遗传解释了这一模式的一部分。

latinEntries.meaning: to inherit; to leave by will

definition_zh: v. 剧烈搅动；（胃）翻腾；n. 搅乳器，制黄油器
definition_en: to move or mix something with great force; a container used to make butter
core_image: 木桶里的牛奶被上下搅动
scene: 暴风雨把海面搅得一片翻滚。 The storm churned the surface of the sea.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：churn 指剧烈搅动；句意是暴风雨把海面搅得翻滚。

pos.zh: 剧烈搅动；翻腾
搅乳器

senses.title: To stir violently
senses.definition: to move or mix something with a strong turning motion
senses.definitionCN: 以强烈的旋转动作移动或混合某物
senses.example: The boat churned the water white.
senses.exampleCN: 船把水搅成白色。
senses.why: The verb comes from the container used to make butter.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词来自打黄油用的容器。

senses.title: The butter maker
senses.definition: a container in which cream is beaten into butter
senses.definitionCN: 把奶油打成黄油的容器
senses.example: The old churn stood in the dairy.

definition_zh: 告诫；警告；责备；劝告；训诫
definition_en: to warn, advise, or criticize someone firmly, usually without anger, so that they avoid a mistake
core_image: 有人在耳边轻敲一下，提醒你别走错
scene: 训练结束后，教练把几名队员叫到一旁，低声说出迟到的问题。 The coach admonished the players for arriving late to training.
sceneCN: 这里 admonish 是「责备、告诫」（第 2 个义项：因过失而温和地批评）；句意为教练因队员训练迟到而责备了他们。图中可辨识物件：训练场、秒表、队服。

senses.title: To warn someone firmly
senses.definition: to warn someone strongly about a danger or a likely mistake, so that they avoid it
senses.definitionCN: 就某种危险或可能的错误强烈提醒某人，使其避开
senses.example: The guide admonished us not to swim beyond the reef.
senses.exampleCN: 向导告诫我们不要游到礁石之外。
senses.why: The word carries a reminder that comes as a tap on the shoulder: the warning arrives before the harm, not after.
senses.whyCN: 这个词带着「肩头被轻敲一下」的提醒：警告在伤害之前到达，而不是之后。

senses.title: To rebuke mildly
senses.definition: to criticize someone for a fault in a quiet, corrective way rather than with anger
senses.definitionCN: 以平静、纠正性的方式批评某人的过失，而不是发怒
senses.example: The teacher admonished the boy for talking during the test.
senses.exampleCN: 老师责备那个男孩考试时讲话。
senses.why: A rebuke here is still a reminder: the fault is named so that it will not be repeated, not to humiliate.
senses.whyCN: 这里的责备仍是一种提醒：指出过失是为了不再重犯，而不是为了羞辱。

senses.title: To remind someone of a duty
senses.definition: to remind a person of a responsibility or an obligation they must not forget
senses.definitionCN: 提醒某人不要忘记某项责任或义务
senses.example: The judge admonished the jury to weigh the evidence carefully.
senses.exampleCN: 法官提醒陪审团仔细权衡证据。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is simply to put something into someone's mind, and a duty is exactly what must be kept there.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层就是「把事情放进某人心里」，而职责正是必须一直放在那里的东西。

senses.title: To urge earnestly
senses.definition: to urge someone seriously to do or avoid something, often in a formal setting
senses.definitionCN: 郑重敦促某人去做或避免某事，常用于正式场合
senses.example: The doctor admonished him to rest for a full week.
senses.exampleCN: 医生郑重劝他休息整整一周。
senses.why: Urging is a warning turned forward: instead of describing the danger, the speaker presses a course of action on the listener.
senses.whyCN: 敦促是把警告转向前方：说话者不再描述危险，而是把某个做法压到听者身上。

senses.title: To counsel morally
senses.definition: to give moral or religious counsel, often from a position of authority
senses.definitionCN: 从权威位置给出道德或宗教上的训导
senses.example: The elder admonished the young men to keep their promises.
senses.exampleCN: 长者训诫年轻人要守信。
senses.why: Authority gives the reminder weight: the same words from a stranger would be advice, but from an elder they are a charge.
senses.whyCN: 权威给提醒增加了分量：同样的话出自陌生人之口只是建议，出自长者之口便成了训诫。

senses.title: To caution against a consequence
senses.definition: to point out the bad consequence that will follow if a warning is ignored
senses.definitionCN: 指出若无视警告将会出现的坏后果
senses.example: The inspector admonished the company against ignoring the safety rules.
senses.exampleCN: 检查员警告该公司不要无视安全规定。
senses.why: The reminder is paired with a forecast: the door is still open, but the speaker describes what lies behind it.
senses.whyCN: 提醒配上了一个预报：门还开着，但说话者描述门后有什么。

senses.title: To issue an official reprimand
senses.definition: to record a formal reprimand, especially in law, employment, or a disciplinary process
senses.definitionCN: 记录正式申诫，多用于法律、雇佣或纪律程序
senses.example: The court admonished the witness for refusing to answer.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭就证人拒答一事对其予以申诫。
senses.why: Once the reminder is written down, a private tap becomes a public record, and the word enters official language.
senses.whyCN: 提醒一旦被写下来，私下的一记轻敲就变成公开记录，这个词也由此进入官方语言。

senses.title: To urge someone to do something
senses.definition: to press someone to carry out an action, in the pattern admonish someone to do something
senses.definitionCN: 以 admonish someone to do something 的结构催促某人采取行动
senses.example: She admonished her brother to call their mother more often.
senses.exampleCN: 她敦促弟弟多给母亲打电话。
senses.why: The reminder has a target: it is not only about what to avoid, but about the act that should now be performed.
senses.whyCN: 提醒有了目标：不只是要避开什么，还包括现在就应该去做的那件事。

intro.en: Admonish comes from a Latin verb of reminding, and its family is full of words about warning, memory and advice.
intro.cn: admonish 来自一个表示「提醒」的拉丁动词，它的词族里满是与警告、记忆和建议有关的词。

items.en: The warning root is often connected with *men-, 'to think, mind', but the reconstruction is not certain.
items.cn: 这个「警告」词根常与 *men-「思考、心智」联系起来，但构拟并不确定。

items.en: Monere meant 'to warn, remind, advise', and it also produced monitor and monument.
items.cn: monere 意为「警告、提醒、建议」，它还生出 monitor 与 monument。

items.en: Ad plus monere formed admonere, 'to remind, warn, urge'. The prefix adds direction rather than intensity.
items.cn: ad 与 monere 构成 admonere，意为「提醒、警告、敦促」。前缀加的是方向，而不是强度。

items.en: Old French amonester carried the word into English, where the Latin d was restored by later spelling.
items.cn: 古法语 amonester 把词带入英语，后来的拼写又恢复了拉丁语的 d。

items.en: The verb appears in the fourteenth century with the senses of warning, advising and reproving already together.
items.cn: 动词于十四世纪出现，警告、建议与责备三个义项当时已经并存。

items.en: Legal and workplace usage adds a formal reprimand, while everyday usage keeps the quiet corrective tone.
items.cn: 法律与职场用法增加了正式申诫一义，日常用法则保留平静纠正的语气。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin warning root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of warning and criticism, which differ in force and in who has the authority to speak.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「警告」词根构成的词；近义组收警告与批评类动词，彼此在力度和说话者权威上不同。

normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁「警告」词根，以及这个动词实际采用的句型。

normal.en: monere means to warn or remind: admonish is a warning aimed at a particular person.
normal.cn: monere 意为「警告、提醒」：admonish 就是对准某个人的警告。

normal.en: The same root gives monitor and monument, both about keeping something in mind.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 monitor 与 monument，两者都与「把某事记在心里」有关。

normal.en: Admonish someone for a fault, and admonish someone against a danger.
normal.cn: 因过失用 admonish someone for，针对危险用 admonish someone against。

normal.en: The -ish here is not the English suffix meaning like; it came from an Old French verb ending.
normal.cn: 这里的 -ish 不是英语中表示「像……」的后缀，它来自古法语动词词尾。

normal.en: Admonish keeps a quiet tone: it corrects without shouting.
normal.cn: admonish 保持平静的语气：它纠正人，但不喊叫。

abstract.en: Picture a hand tapping a shoulder just before a step is taken, not after the fall.
abstract.cn: 想象一只的手在迈步之前轻拍肩膀，而不是在摔倒之后。

abstract.en: The tap is the same whether it warns, reminds or reproves: someone is being steered back to the right line.
abstract.cn: 这记轻拍无论是警告、提醒还是责备都一样：有人在被引回正确的线上。

abstract.en: A written admonition is that tap turned into ink, which is why courts and employers can use it.
abstract.cn: 书面的 admonition 就是那记轻拍变成了墨迹，所以法庭和雇主都能使用它。

examples.en: The ranger admonished the hikers to carry enough water.

examples.en: She was admonished for leaving the laboratory unlocked.

examples.en: His letter admonished the committee against a hasty decision.
examples.cn: 他的信告诫委员会不要仓促作出决定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德莫尼什」——阿德敲桌提醒：告诫、责备

root: 拉丁语 ad-（朝向）+ monere（警告、提醒）构成 admonere，字面为「对着某人提醒」，故有告诫、劝告与温和责备三义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of admonish all deliver the same reminder in different settings: a danger to avoid, a fault to correct, a duty to keep, a course to follow, a moral charge, a consequence, an official record, or an act to perform.
sensesIntro.cn: admonish 的八个义项都在不同场合递出同一份提醒：要避开的危险、要纠正的过失、要记住的职责、要遵循的做法、道德上的训导、不良后果、官方记录，或应当去做的事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand taps a shoulder at the edge of a wrong step and points back to the right line.
core.cn: 核心意象：在即将迈错的一步边上，一只手轻拍肩膀，把人指回正确的线。

branches.en: THE DANGER LINE: the reminder arrives before harm and describes what waits if it is ignored.
branches.cn: 危险线：提醒在伤害之前到达，并说明若被无视会有什么等着。

branches.en: THE FAULT LINE: a fault already committed is named calmly so that it is not repeated.
branches.cn: 过失线：已经犯下的过失被平静地点出，为的是不再重犯。

branches.en: THE DUTY LINE: authority keeps a responsibility or a moral charge in the listener's mind.
branches.cn: 职责线：权威把某项责任或道德训导留在听者心里。

branches.en: THE ACTION LINE: the warning turns forward and presses a particular act on the listener.
branches.cn: 行动线：警告转向前方，把某个具体行动压到听者身上。

branches.en: THE RECORD LINE: the private tap becomes a written reprimand inside an institution.
branches.cn: 记录线：私下的一记轻敲变成机构内部的书面申诫。

intro.en: Admonish is a Latin prefix plus a Latin warning verb, with an Old French verb ending; English adds the noun and adjective suffixes.
intro.cn: admonish 由拉丁语前缀、拉丁「警告」动词和古法语动词词尾构成；英语再加入名词与形容词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Monere, admonere and admonitio are recorded in Latin, so no part of the core is reconstructed except the deeper Indo-European root.
latinIntro.cn: monere、admonere 与 admonitio 在拉丁语中都有记录，除更早的印欧词根外，核心部分都不属重构。

items.example: It aims the warning at a particular person.
items.exampleCN: 它把警告对准某个具体的人。

items.example: It is the warning root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一词族的「警告」词根。

items.example: The compound is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: It is not the English suffix meaning like.
items.exampleCN: 它并不是英语中表示「像……」的后缀。

items.example: It forms admonition.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 admonition。

items.example: It forms admonitory.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 admonitory。

items.example: It forms admonishment.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 admonishment。

items.example: It forms admonisher.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 admonisher。

derivatives.zh: 由词干加 -ition 构成，义为「告诫；警告」
由词干加 -ory 构成，义为「警告性的」
由动词加 -ment 构成，义为「训诫」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「告诫者」

definition_zh: 总体上、一般说来；就整体而言（允许个别例外）
definition_en: usually; considering the whole rather than details or exceptions
core_image: 一只手掌摊开，五根手指整体朝上，指缝间还留有空隙
scene: 市场调查员翻完整本记录，说多数顾客满意，但也指出投诉集中在退换货。 Customers are satisfied in general, though returns remain a sore point.
sceneCN: 这里取「总体上、一般说来」（第 1 个义项：就整体而言，允许例外）；句意为顾客总体满意，但退货仍是痛点。

pos.zh: 副词短语：总体上；一般说来

senses.title: The broad view
senses.definition: used to state what is true of a whole group, while allowing individual exceptions
senses.definitionCN: 用来陈述对整个群体成立的情况，同时容许个别例外
senses.example: In general, the climate is mild, but winters can be harsh.
senses.exampleCN: 总体而言气候温和，但冬季可能严寒。
senses.why: General belongs to the whole kind, so the phrase speaks for the group rather than for each member.
senses.whyCN: 这个词属于整个类别，因此短语代表群体说话，而非逐个成员。

senses.title: Beside the single adverb
senses.titleCN: 语法边界：与单词副词的分工
senses.definition: the frame stands as a sentence adverbial, while the single adverb often sits inside the clause
senses.definitionCN: 这个框架作句子状语，而单词副词常位于小句内部
senses.example: Prices in general have risen faster than wages.
senses.exampleCN: 物价总体上涨得比工资快。
senses.why: A sentence-level comment differs from a manner adverb attached to one verb.
senses.whyCN: 句子层面的评述不同于依附单个动词的方式副词。

senses.title: Against one case
senses.titleCN: 对照义：与个别突出相对
senses.definition: it states the wide pattern, and the contrasting phrase then selects the exception
senses.definitionCN: 它陈述宽泛的格局，对照短语随后挑出例外
senses.example: In general the plan is sound; in particular the budget needs work.
senses.exampleCN: 总体看方案稳妥，尤其是预算还需加工。
senses.why: A pattern needs a contrast to be useful, and the pair supplies both ends.
senses.whyCN: 格局需要对照才有用，这一对短语正好提供两端。

senses.title: The sentence opener
senses.definition: at the start of a sentence it warns the reader that a summary follows
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，提示读者接下来是概括
senses.example: In general, students prefer morning classes.
senses.exampleCN: 一般说来，学生更喜欢上午的课。
senses.why: Opening position sets the frame before the detail arrives, which is why summaries begin this way.
senses.whyCN: 前置位置在细节到来前先设好框架，因此概括常这样开头。

senses.title: True with exceptions
senses.titleCN: 例外义：大体成立但有例外
senses.definition: it claims a tendency, not a law, and so leaves room for cases that do not fit
senses.definitionCN: 它主张一种倾向而非定律，因此给不合的例子留了余地
senses.example: The machine is reliable in general, yet it fails in cold weather.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器总体可靠，却在寒冷天气里失灵。
senses.why: A tendency can be real without covering every instance, and the phrase marks exactly that strength.
senses.whyCN: 倾向可以真实存在而不覆盖每一例，这个短语标的正是那种力度。

senses.title: Like a whole-view phrase
senses.titleCN: 近义辨析：与整体评说相近
senses.definition: it resembles the phrase meaning on the whole, though it sounds slightly more formal and abstract
senses.definitionCN: 它与表整体评说的短语相近，只是听来更正式、更抽象
senses.example: In general, the two accounts agree.
senses.exampleCN: 总体而言，两种叙述是一致的。
senses.why: Both weigh the whole, but one sounds like a judgement and the other like a summary.
senses.whyCN: 两者都权衡整体，但一个像判断，另一个像概述。

senses.title: A whole group of people
senses.titleCN: 群体义：指某一类人的整体
senses.definition: placed after a plural noun it means the members of that group taken together
senses.definitionCN: 放在复数名词之后，指该群体的成员合起来看
senses.example: People in general are wary of sudden changes.
senses.exampleCN: 一般人对突然的变化都心存戒备。
senses.why: Here the phrase works inside a noun phrase, showing that general can attach to a group as well as to a clause.
senses.whyCN: 此处短语位于名词短语内部，说明这个词既能挂在小句上，也能挂在群体上。

senses.title: Not the military rank
senses.definition: the noun can name an officer of high rank, but the phrase only makes a broad statement
senses.definitionCN: 这个名词可指高级军官，但短语只作宽泛陈述
senses.example: In general marks a broad view, not a military rank.
senses.exampleCN: 总体而言一语标的是宽泛视角，不是军衔。
senses.why: The rank sense grew from the adjective, and the fixed phrase kept only the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 军衔义由形容词发展而来，固定短语只保留形容词义。

intro.en: General comes from Latin generalis, belonging to a whole kind, from genus, kind or stock. The Latin chain is secure; the phrase is modern.
intro.cn: general 来自拉丁语 generalis「属于整个类别的」，词根 genus 意为种类、族属。拉丁语链条清楚；短语属近代。

items.en: Genus named a kind, a race or a stock, and it stands behind generation and genre as well.
items.cn: genus 指种类、族属或血统，也支撑着 generation 与 genre 等词。

items.en: The adjective marked what applies to the whole kind rather than to one member.
items.cn: 这个形容词标出适用于整个类别而非单个成员的东西。

items.en: French used the word for common or universal before English borrowed it.
items.cn: 法语先用这个词表共同、普遍，英语随后借入。

items.en: A commander of the whole force took the adjective as a title, giving the military noun.
items.cn: 统领全军者以这个形容词为称号，由此产生军衔名词。

items.en: The summarising frame belongs to modern prose; first dates are approximate.
items.cn: 这个概括框架属于近代文字，首见年代为约数。

note.en: The first group shares the root or the summarising job but differs in grammar or scope; the second group are adverbs and phrases of broad statement.
note.cn: 第一组共用词根或概括功能，但语法或范围不同；第二组是表宽泛陈述的副词与短语。

entries.definition: It usually modifies a verb and means normally.
entries.definitionCN: 通常修饰动词，意为一般地。

entries.definition: It means stated broadly, without figures.
entries.definitionCN: 意为笼统陈述，不给具体数字。

entries.definition: It means for the most part, slightly literary.
entries.definitionCN: 意为大体上，略偏书面。

entries.definition: It treats something as one unit rather than as members.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物当作一个整体，而非各个成员。

entries.definition: A judgement after balancing the parts.
entries.definitionCN: 权衡各部分之后作出的判断。

entries.definition: It marks a statement made at a wide angle.
entries.definitionCN: 标出从宽泛角度作出的陈述。

entries.definition: It concerns how often, not how widely.
entries.definitionCN: 说的是频次，而非覆盖面。

entries.definition: A conversational way to say mostly.
entries.definitionCN: 口语中表大体上。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real kind-root, the later military title and the real grammar of sentence adverbial and postposed group.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实的种类词根、后来的军衔称号，以及句子状语与后置群体的真实语法。

normal.en: A kind is a whole class, so the phrase speaks for the class, not each member.
normal.cn: 种类是整个类别，因此短语为类别说话，而非逐个成员。

normal.en: A sentence adverbial frames the claim, while a manner adverb touches one verb.
normal.cn: 句子状语为陈述设框，方式副词只碰一个动词。

normal.en: A tendency can be true without covering every case.
normal.cn: 倾向可以成立，而不覆盖每一例。

normal.en: After a plural noun, it gathers the members into one body.
normal.cn: 放在复数名词后，它把成员聚成一个整体。

normal.en: The rank came from the adjective, and the frame kept only the adjective.
normal.cn: 军衔来自形容词，而这个框架只保留形容词。

abstract.en: Like an open palm seen from above: five fingers counted as one hand.
abstract.cn: 像从上方看一只摊开的手掌：五根指头算作一只手。

abstract.en: Like a map at a wide zoom, where streets vanish and the shape of the country shows.
abstract.cn: 像缩小很多的地图：街道消失，国形显现。

abstract.en: Like a group photograph in which no single face is the subject.
abstract.cn: 像一张合影，其中没有哪张脸是主角。

examples.en: In general, the soil here drains quickly.
examples.cn: 总体而言，这里的土壤排水很快。

examples.en: The staff in general welcomed the change.
examples.cn: 员工总体上欢迎这一变动。

examples.en: In general, the older buildings need more repair.
examples.cn: 一般说来，较旧的建筑需要更多维修。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「因 健若」——摊开的手掌，五根指头算作一只手：总体上

root: 核心形容词意为总体的，出自拉丁语 generalis「属于整个类别的」，词根 genus 意为种类、族属。该短语表总体上为近代定型，首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses separate the broad view, the boundary against the adverb, the contrast with one case, the sentence opener, truth with exceptions, the near twin, a whole group of people and the exclusion of the military rank.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项区分：总体视角、与副词的语法边界、与个别案例的对照、句首开篇、容许例外、近义整体评说、指群体整体，以及排除军衔义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open palm seen from above, five fingers counted together as one hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：从上方看一只摊开的手掌，五根指头合起来算一只手。

branches.en: THE SUMMARY: a whole class is described before any detail arrives.
branches.cn: 概括：在细节到来前先描述整个类别。

branches.en: THE GRAMMAR: a sentence adverbial frames a claim, unlike an adverb on one verb.
branches.cn: 语法：句子状语为陈述设框，不同于依附单个动词的副词。

branches.en: THE CONTRASTS: an exception can be selected, and no military rank is meant.
branches.cn: 对照：可以挑出例外，且不指军衔。

branches.en: THE STRENGTH: a tendency holds without covering every case.
branches.cn: 力度：倾向成立而不覆盖每一例。

branches.en: THE GROUP: after a plural noun the phrase gathers the members together.
branches.cn: 群体：放在复数名词后，把成员聚在一起。

intro.en: The phrase rests on a Latin adjective of a whole kind, whose root for kind is shared across many English words.
intro.cn: 这个短语建在一个表整个类别的拉丁语形容词上，其种类词根为许多英语词共用。

latinIntro.en: Latin genus, kind, gives generalis, of the whole kind; English also took the noun as a military title.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 genus「种类」给出 generalis「属于整个类别的」；英语还把这个名词用作军衔称号。

items.example: The root also stands behind generation and genre.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也支撑着世代与体裁等词。

items.example: The adjective speaks for the class rather than one member.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词为类别而非单个成员说话。

items.example: English keeps the adjective and adds the rank.
items.exampleCN: 英语保留形容词，又加上军衔。

items.example: The adverb marks a normal pattern.
items.exampleCN: 副词标出通常的格局。

items.example: The verb turns one case into a class.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把一个案例变成一类。

items.example: The noun names the resulting broad claim.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指由此产生的宽泛主张。

items.example: The noun measures how wide a statement is.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词衡量陈述有多宽。

items.example: The suffix names the office or the skill.
items.exampleCN: 后缀指职位或才能。

items.example: The frame is standard in summary.
items.exampleCN: 这个框架是概括的标准形式。

definition_zh: 由血缘与婚姻关系连接起来、可以互相往来的亲属群体
definition_en: the web of relatives linked by blood or marriage through whom people exchange help, information and obligations
core_image: 一张手绘的族谱铺在桌上，线条从一对老人向四周伸开，每个节点都连着另一户人家的门
scene: 祠堂的墙上挂着一张很大的族谱，红线和黑线把几十户人家连在一起。 A kinship network links these farmers to cousins in three neighbouring counties.
sceneCN: 这里 kinship network 指「由血缘与婚姻连接、可彼此往来的亲属群体」（第 1 个义项：一张以亲属关系为线的互助之网）；句意为这张亲属网络把这些农户与三个邻县的表亲连在一起。可辨识物件：族谱、红线、黑线、祠堂、门牌。

pos.zh: 亲属网络（名词短语）
人类学中的亲属关系体系

senses.title: Relatives linked by blood or marriage
senses.titleCN: 由血缘或婚姻连接的亲属整体
senses.definition: the whole set of relatives connected to a person through descent or marriage
senses.definitionCN: 通过血缘或婚姻与某人连在一起的全部亲属
senses.example: Anthropologists mapped the kinship network before asking about land use.
senses.exampleCN: 人类学家先画出亲属网络，再询问土地利用情况。
senses.why: kin names the family stock, and network turns it into a set of links rather than a list of names.
senses.whyCN: kin 指家族血脉，network 则把它变成一组联结，而非一串名字。

senses.title: The extended family beyond the household
senses.titleCN: 超出小家庭的扩展亲属
senses.definition: the relatives who live outside one's own house but remain part of daily obligation
senses.definitionCN: 不住在自己家中、却仍属日常义务范围的亲属
senses.example: A child in that village is raised by the wider kinship network.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个村庄里，孩子由更广的亲属网络共同抚养。
senses.why: a household is small, and the network is precisely what lies beyond its walls.
senses.whyCN: 家庭很小，而亲属网络恰恰指墙外的那些关系。

senses.title: A system of kinship terms
senses.definition: the set of words a language uses to distinguish cousins, in-laws and generations
senses.definitionCN: 一种语言用来区分表亲、姻亲与辈分的整套称谓
senses.example: The language encodes the kinship network in separate words for cross-cousins.
senses.exampleCN: 这种语言用不同的词称呼交叉表亲，把亲属网络编进词汇。
senses.why: terms are the map a society draws of its own links.
senses.whyCN: 称谓是社会为自己那些联结画出的地图。

senses.title: A source of everyday support
senses.titleCN: 日常互助与照护的来源
senses.definition: the flow of food, labour and care that relatives give one another in hard times
senses.definitionCN: 困难时期亲属之间输送食物、劳力与照护的流动
senses.example: When the harvest failed, the kinship network supplied grain and labour.
senses.exampleCN: 收成失败时，亲属网络提供了粮食与劳力。
senses.why: links are kept alive by use, so support is the working part of the network.
senses.whyCN: 联结靠使用而存活，因此互助就是这张网真正运转的部分。

senses.title: A channel for inheritance and ritual duty
senses.titleCN: 继承与仪式义务的通道
senses.definition: the route along which property, names and ritual obligations pass from one generation to the next
senses.definitionCN: 财产、名分与仪式义务代代相传所沿的路径
senses.example: Ritual obligations pass along the kinship network rather than the household.
senses.exampleCN: 仪式义务沿着亲属网络传递，而不是沿家庭传递。
senses.why: inheritance and rites are where links become legally and morally binding.
senses.whyCN: 继承与仪式正是联结获得法律与道德约束力的地方。

senses.title: A route for jobs, loans and news
senses.titleCN: 求职、借贷与消息的渠道
senses.definition: the use of relatives as trusted contacts for employment, credit and information
senses.definitionCN: 把亲属当作求职、信贷与消息的可信联系人
senses.example: Migrants found work through a kinship network rather than an agency.
senses.exampleCN: 外来务工者通过亲属网络而非中介找到工作。
senses.why: a web of trusted ties moves resources that formal institutions cannot reach.
senses.whyCN: 由信任联结成的网能输送正式机构触及不到的资源。

senses.title: A web that shrinks in cities
senses.titleCN: 城市化中收缩的亲属网络
senses.definition: the thinning of regular contact among relatives under long commutes and rented flats
senses.definitionCN: 在长途通勤与租住公寓条件下亲属往来逐渐变稀
senses.example: Flat doors and long commutes leave the kinship network thin.
senses.exampleCN: 单元门与长途通勤使亲属网络变得稀薄。
senses.why: distance and time cost links, and a network with no visits fades.
senses.whyCN: 距离与时间消耗联结，无人走访的网络会逐渐消失。

senses.title: Links kept across borders
senses.definition: the maintenance of family ties by phone, remittance and return visits after migration
senses.definitionCN: 迁移之后靠电话、汇款与回乡探访维持的家庭关系
senses.example: Phone calls and remittances hold the kinship network across two continents.
senses.exampleCN: 电话与汇款把亲属网络维系在两个大陆之间。
senses.why: cheap communication lets an old web survive migration instead of breaking.
senses.whyCN: 廉价的通信让旧网在迁移中存续，而不是断裂。

intro.en: Kinship network joins two native Germanic words: kin, from Old English cynn 'family, race', and network, from net plus work. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: kinship network 由两个本族日耳曼语词合成：kin 来自古英语 cynn「家族、族类」，network 由 net 与 work 构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cynn meant 'family, race, kind' and is related to kind. The pre-Germanic shape is reconstructed, so the older form is not witnessed in any text.
items.cn: cynn 意为「家族、族类、种类」，与 kind 同源。日耳曼语之前的形态属重构形式，没有任何文本书证。

items.en: The suffix -scipe made abstract nouns of state or condition, giving kinship the sense 'the condition of being kin'.
items.cn: 后缀 -scipe 构成表状态或状况的抽象名词，使 kinship 获得「身为亲属的状态」之义。

items.en: Net(t) named a mesh of cords, and weorc named work or deed; the compound network first named a mesh of lines, then any connected set.
items.cn: net(t) 指绳线结成的网，weorc 指劳作或行为；复合词 network 先指线网，后指任何相互连接的一整套。

items.en: In the twentieth century network was applied to people, and kinship network named a web of relatives rather than a list of names.
items.cn: 二十世纪，network 被用于人，kinship network 由此指一张亲属之网，而非一串名字。

items.en: Social anthropology made the phrase a technical term for the links a society recognizes, uses and transmits.
items.cn: 社会人类学把这个短语变成术语，指一个社会所承认、使用并传递的联结。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Germanic origin): the older Germanic shape of cynn is reconstructed, and no single first use of the full phrase is recorded.
items.cn: 来源不确定（日耳曼语之前的来源）：cynn 更早的日耳曼语形态属重构形式，整个短语也没有确切的最早书证。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like or are built from kin; group two holds terms for a family group organized on another principle.
note.cn: 第一组是形似 kin 或由 kin 构成的词；第二组是按另一种原则组织家庭群体的词。

entries.definition: Kin plus the collective suffix -red: the relatives taken together, often with a shared ancestor.
entries.definitionCN: kin 加集体后缀 -red：聚在一起、常共有一祖先的亲属。

entries.definition: The abstract relation of being kin; a kinship network is the concrete set of links built from it.
entries.definitionCN: 指身为亲属的抽象关系；亲属网络则是由此建成的具体联结集合。

entries.definition: Relationship through marriage rather than blood, from Latin affinis 'neighbouring'.
entries.definitionCN: 指因婚姻而非血缘形成的关系，来自拉丁 affinis「邻近的」。

entries.definition: A set of connected points of any kind; only the modifier kin makes it a family web.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何相互连接的点集；只有前面的 kin 才使它成为亲属之网。

entries.definition: The relatives beyond the nuclear household treated as one group; the network stresses how they are connected.
entries.definitionCN: 指核心家庭之外的亲属整体；网络一词强调他们如何相连。

entries.definition: A large group claiming descent from one ancestor, often with a common name; a network need not share a name.
entries.definitionCN: 指自称出自同一祖先的大型群体，常共用名号；亲属网络则不必共用名号。

entries.definition: A single traced line of ancestors and descendants; a network contains many such lines at once.
entries.definitionCN: 指一条可追溯的世代传承线；亲属网络同时包含多条这样的线。

entries.definition: A web of people linked by friendship, work or interest; kinship network limits the links to relatives.
entries.definitionCN: 指由友谊、工作或兴趣连成的人际网；亲属网络则把联结限定在亲属之间。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: kin is the family stock; -ship turns it into the state of being related.
normal.cn: kin 指家族血脉；-ship 把它变成「有亲属关系」这一状态。

normal.en: network is literally net plus work: a mesh that does the work of connecting people.
normal.cn: network 字面是 net 加 work：一张承担连接工作的网。

normal.en: The same kin root appears in kinsman, kinswoman and kinfolk.
normal.cn: 同一 kin 词根出现在 kinsman、kinswoman 与 kinfolk 中。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: dense kinship network, extended kinship network, kinship network support.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：稠密的亲属网络、扩展的亲属网络、亲属网络的支持。

normal.en: Anthropology uses the phrase for links that are recognized, not merely biological.
normal.cn: 人类学用这个短语指被社会承认的联结，而不只是生物学上的关系。

abstract.en: Picture a map where every road ends at someone's kitchen door.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，每条路的尽头都是某户人家的厨房门口。

abstract.en: Picture a rope bridge whose planks are visits, calls and shared meals.
abstract.cn: 想象一座绳桥，桥板是一次次走访、电话与共餐。

abstract.en: Picture a net that holds grain in a bad year and lets it travel in a good one.
abstract.cn: 想象一张网，荒年兜住粮食，丰年又让粮食流动。

examples.en: The kinship network decided who would host the wedding feast.
examples.cn: 亲属网络决定了由谁来承办婚宴。

examples.en: A dense kinship network can soften the shock of a factory closure.
examples.cn: 稠密的亲属网络能缓冲工厂倒闭带来的冲击。

examples.en: Researchers asked how migration had changed the kinship network.
examples.cn: 研究者询问迁徙如何改变了亲属网络。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「kin（亲属）+ ship（船/关系）+ net（网）」——亲属像一张大网上的船，彼此连着

root: kin 来自古英语 cynn「家族、族类」，与 kind 同源；-ship 来自古英语 -scipe，表状态；network 为 net「网」+ work「劳作」的英语复合词。日耳曼语之前的形态均属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one structure: a set of links created by blood and marriage, which is then read as a group, a vocabulary, a support system, an inheritance channel, a job market, a shrinking city web and a web stretched across borders.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个结构展开：由血缘与婚姻造成的一组联结，再依次被读作一个群体、一套称谓、一套互助系统、一条继承通道、一个求职渠道、一张城市中收缩的网，以及一张跨境的网。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand-drawn family tree lying on a table, every branch ending at another household's door.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张手绘族谱铺在桌上，每条分支的尽头都是另一户人家的门。

branches.en: THE WEB ITSELF: the phrase names the whole set of links before it names any use of them.
branches.cn: 网本身：这个短语先指全部联结，再指这些联结的任何用途。

branches.en: OUTSIDE THE WALL AND IN THE LANGUAGE: the same links appear as relatives beyond the house and as words for those relatives.
branches.cn: 墙外与语言中：同一组联结既表现为屋外的亲属，也表现为称呼他们的词。

branches.en: CARE AND TRANSMISSION: food and labour flow one way, names and duties the other.
branches.cn: 照护与传承：食物与劳力向一个方向流动，名分与义务向另一个方向流动。

branches.en: TRUST AS CAPITAL: relatives become references, lenders and messengers.
branches.cn: 信任作资本：亲属变成担保人、放贷者与传信人。

branches.en: DISTANCE TESTS THE WEB: the city thins it, and migration either breaks it or stretches it.
branches.cn: 距离考验这张网：城市使它变稀，迁徙则要么扯断它，要么把它拉长。

intro.en: Both halves of the phrase are native Germanic material, so the family is read through stems and suffixes rather than Latin roots.
intro.cn: 这个短语的两半都是本族日耳曼语材料，因此要按词干与后缀来读，而非按拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: No Latin borrowing stands behind this phrase; the morphemes are Old English, so no Latin source forms are recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 这个短语背后没有拉丁借词，其语素来自古英语，因此不列拉丁语源形式。

items.example: Cynn is the ancestor of kin and kind.
items.exampleCN: cynn 是 kin 与 kind 的祖先形式。

items.example: Kin can mean one relative or the whole family.
items.exampleCN: kin 既可指一位亲属，也可指整个家族。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun into a state.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成一种状态。

items.example: Kinship is the relation before it is an organisation.
items.exampleCN: kinship 先是关系，后才成为一种组织。

items.example: A net holds things by connecting them.
items.exampleCN: 网通过连接来兜住东西。

items.example: Weorc gives English work.
items.exampleCN: weorc 衍生出英语 work。

items.meaning: a connected mesh; later any linked set
items.meaningCN: 相连的网；后指任何互联集合
items.example: The compound moved from cords to people.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词从绳线扩展到了人。

items.example: Kinsman keeps the old root alive.
items.exampleCN: kinsman 让古老词根延续下来。

items.example: Networking applies the mesh image to careers.
items.exampleCN: networking 把网的形象用于职业关系。

definition_zh: 语言的；语言学的；与语言运用有关的
definition_en: relating to language or to the scientific study of language
core_image: 一页写满分句与箭头的手稿，句子之间用细线连起，页边标着几个小号数
scene: 书桌上摊着一页写满分句与箭头的手稿，句子之间用细线相连。 The editors examined linguistic clues before they dated the manuscript.
sceneCN: 这里指「与语言特征有关的」（第 1 个义项：涉及语言本身的）；句意为编者在为手稿定年之前，先检查了语言线索。可辨识物件：手稿、分句、箭头、细线。

pos.zh: 语言的；语言学的

senses.title: Relating to language itself
senses.definition: concerning the sounds, words and grammar of a language
senses.definitionCN: 涉及一种语言的声音、词汇与语法
senses.example: Linguistic change is usually gradual rather than sudden.
senses.exampleCN: 语言变化通常是渐进的，而不是突然的。
senses.why: the adjective simply attaches the Latin word for language to any feature of it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把拉丁语表「语言」的词挂到语言的任何特征上。

senses.title: Relating to the discipline of linguistics
senses.definition: belonging to the scientific study of language as a field
senses.definitionCN: 属于把语言作为研究对象的科学领域
senses.example: The paper appeared in a linguistic journal, not a literary one.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文发表在一份语言学刊物上，而非文学刊物。
senses.why: the noun for the field and the adjective for it differ by one ending, so the same description covers both language and its study.
senses.whyCN: 学科名词与它的形容词只差一个词尾，因此同一描述既覆盖语言，也覆盖对语言的研究。

senses.title: Inner knowledge of grammar
senses.titleCN: 说话者内在的语法知识
senses.definition: describing the tacit knowledge a speaker has of the rules of a language
senses.definitionCN: 描述说话者对某一语言规则的默会知识
senses.example: Children's linguistic competence grows faster than their vocabulary lists suggest.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童的语言能力增长得比词汇表所显示的更快。
senses.why: the discipline drew a line between what a speaker knows and what a speaker does.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科在「说话者知道什么」与「说话者做什么」之间划了一条线。

senses.title: A minority defined by its tongue
senses.titleCN: 以语言划分的少数群体
senses.definition: naming a community distinguished by the language it speaks
senses.definitionCN: 指以所说语言而区分出来的群体
senses.example: Linguistic minorities won the right to local schooling.
senses.exampleCN: 语言少数群体争取到了地方办学的权利。
senses.why: a community can be marked out by the tongue it uses, and the adjective follows that marker.
senses.whyCN: 一个群体可以由其所用语言标记出来，形容词便跟着这个标记走。

senses.title: Variety across languages
senses.definition: describing the range of different languages and their features
senses.definitionCN: 描述不同语言及其特征的分布范围
senses.example: The region's linguistic diversity is greater than its biological diversity.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的语言多样性超过它的生物多样性。
senses.why: counting different tongues turns the adjective into a word about range.
senses.whyCN: 把不同语言计数，就让这个形容词变成关于「范围」的词。

senses.title: Classification by structure
senses.definition: used of the comparison and classification of language structures
senses.definitionCN: 用于语言结构的比较与分类
senses.example: Linguistic typology groups languages by how they build sentences.
senses.exampleCN: 语言类型学按造句方式给语言分组。
senses.why: to compare structures is to classify them, and classification is another face of the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 比较结构就是给结构分类，而分类是这个形容词的另一副面孔。

senses.title: A barrier caused by language
senses.definition: describing an obstacle that arises because people do not share a tongue
senses.definitionCN: 描述因人们不共用一种语言而产生的障碍
senses.example: The linguistic barrier mattered more than the border itself.
senses.exampleCN: 语言障碍比边界本身更要紧。
senses.why: where tongues differ, communication can fail, so the adjective also names an obstacle.
senses.whyCN: 语言不同处，交流可能失败，因此这个形容词也指障碍。

senses.title: Wording used as evidence
senses.definition: describing features of wording that can identify or date a text
senses.definitionCN: 描述可用于识别或为文本定年的措辞特征
senses.example: Linguistic evidence placed the letter in the late sixteenth century.
senses.exampleCN: 语言证据把这封信定在十六世纪后期。
senses.why: wording leaves traces that can be read, so the adjective moves from language to evidence.
senses.whyCN: 措辞留下可读的痕迹，因此这个形容词从语言转到证据。

intro.en: Linguistic is a nineteenth-century adjective built on Latin lingua 'tongue, language' with the ending -isticus, probably through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词是十九世纪形成的形容词，建在拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」之上，带拉丁形容词词尾，很可能经法语传入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lingua meant 'tongue' and 'language'; its deeper origin is unsettled and is not demonstrated by any attested older form.
items.cn: lingua 兼指「舌头」与「语言」；其更深来源无定论，也没有任何可证实的更早形式。

items.en: The ending -isticus, taken from Greek, built adjectives meaning 'of or relating to a practice or field'.
items.cn: 这个源自希腊语的词尾构成形容词，意为「属于或关于某实践或领域的」。

items.en: French formed linguistique for the study of language in the early nineteenth century, and English took the adjective soon after.
items.cn: 法语在十九世纪初为语言研究造出相应形容词，英语随后借入。

items.en: As linguistics became a university subject, the adjective came to mean both 'of language' and 'of the discipline'.
items.cn: 随着语言学成为大学学科，这个形容词既指「语言的」，也指「语言学的」。

items.en: The twentieth century added phrases such as linguistic minority and linguistic evidence, extending the adjective into law and history.
items.cn: 二十世纪增加了「语言少数群体」「语言证据」等说法，把这个形容词扩展到法律与历史领域。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of the root is unknown, and the exact first English printing of the adjective is not documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定：该词根在拉丁语之前的来源不明，这个形容词最早的英语印刷记录亦无确切文献。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root words that are easily swapped for the adjective; group two holds adjectives describing language matters.
note.cn: 第一组是同根、容易与这个形容词混用的词；第二组是描述语言事务的形容词。

entries.definition: The name of the discipline; the adjective describes something within it.
entries.definitionCN: 指学科名称；形容词则描述该学科之内的事物。

entries.definition: A person who studies language; it is a noun for a doer.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究语言的人，是表施动者的名词。

entries.definition: The system itself; the adjective cannot stand for the system.
entries.definitionCN: 指系统本身；形容词不能替代那个系统。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'of the tongue' in anatomy or dentistry, not 'of language'.
entries.definitionCN: 在解剖与牙科中指「舌的」，而非「语言的」。

entries.definition: Relating to words as opposed to actions; it does not refer to grammar or language systems.
entries.definitionCN: 指以词语而非行动表达，不涉及语法或语言系统。

entries.definition: Concerned with meaning rather than structure; it is one part of what linguistic covers.
entries.definitionCN: 关注意义而非结构，是语言研究覆盖的一部分。

entries.definition: Concerned with grammar or with whether a sentence is well formed.
entries.definitionCN: 关注语法或句子是否合式。

entries.definition: Relating to the older study of texts and languages; it is historical where linguistic is general.
entries.definitionCN: 指较旧的文本与语言考据之学，偏历史，而「语言的」更宽泛。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The adjective carries the same root as the noun for tongue, so it always points back to speech.
normal.cn: 这个形容词与表「舌头」的名词共享词根，因此总指向言语。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the fields: linguistic diversity, linguistic evidence, linguistic minority.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示领域：语言多样性、语言证据、语言少数群体。

normal.en: The adverb adds a manner: linguistically speaking.
normal.cn: 副词加上方式：从语言上说。

normal.en: The family runs language, linguist, linguistics, bilingual, multilingual.
normal.cn: 同族包括「语言」「语言学家」「语言学」「双语的」「多语的」。

normal.en: A text marked with arrows between clauses is the picture to keep.
normal.cn: 在分句之间画箭头的那页文本，是要留住的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a fingerprint made of vowels instead of ridges.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚由元音而非纹路组成的指纹。

abstract.en: Picture a map whose borders follow the spread of words.
abstract.cn: 想象一张边界沿着词语传播而画的图。

abstract.en: Picture a fence built between two villages out of untranslated signs.
abstract.cn: 想象两个村子之间用无法翻译的标牌搭成的一道栅栏。

examples.en: Linguistic differences often survive political union by centuries.
examples.cn: 语言差异常常在政治统一之后还延续几个世纪。

examples.en: The court accepted linguistic analysis as evidence of authorship.
examples.cn: 法庭接受语言分析作为作者身份的证据。

examples.en: Linguistic minorities asked for bilingual ballots.
examples.cn: 语言少数群体要求提供双语选票。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「林归斯提克」——林子里归拢来的那套说话规矩，就是语言的。

root: 拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」加源自希腊语的形容词词尾构成，十九世纪经法语进入英语，指「语言的」，后也指「语言学的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all attach the adjective to a different object: the language itself, the discipline, the speaker's inner rules, a community, a range of tongues, a classification, a barrier and a piece of evidence.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把这个形容词挂到不同对象上：语言本身、学科、说话者的内在规则、一个群体、语言的范围、一种分类、一道障碍以及一份证据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a manuscript page where clauses are linked by thin arrows.
core.cn: 核心意象：一页手稿，分句之间用细箭头相连。

branches.en: THE SIMPLEST LINK: any feature of a language can take the adjective.
branches.cn: 最简单的连接：语言的任何特征都能带这个形容词。

branches.en: THE FIELD: the same adjective also marks work done inside the discipline.
branches.cn: 学科：同一个形容词也标记学科内部的研究。

branches.en: INSIDE THE SPEAKER: tacit grammatical knowledge is a linguistic fact too.
branches.cn: 说话者之内：默会的语法知识同样是语言事实。

branches.en: GROUPS AND RANGES: communities are defined by tongues, and tongues differ widely.
branches.cn: 群体与范围：社群由语言界定，而语言彼此差异很大。

branches.en: ORDER, OBSTACLE, PROOF: structure can be classified, difference can block, and wording can testify.
branches.cn: 秩序、障碍与证据：结构可被分类，差异会成阻碍，而措辞可以提供证明。

intro.en: The word is a Latin-rooted adjective with a Greek-derived ending, so it can be read as root plus ending.
intro.cn: 这是一个带拉丁词根与希腊来源词尾的形容词，可按「词根加词尾」来读。

latinIntro.en: Latin lingua supplies the root; the ending came into Latin from Greek and later built many English adjectives of fields and practices.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lingua 提供词根；词尾经拉丁语来自希腊语，后来构成许多英语中表领域与实践的形容词。

items.example: The root ties every sense back to speech.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根把每个义项都系回言语。

items.structure: Greek-derived ending via Latin, 'of or relating to'

definition_zh: n. 残疾；伤残；障碍；（法律）无行为能力
definition_en: a physical or mental condition that limits movements, senses or activities; also a legal disqualification

scene: 她从不把残疾当成障碍。 She never treats her disability as a barrier.
sceneCN: 这里 disability 是「残疾」（第 1 个义项：限制日常活动的身体或心智状况）；句意是她从不把残疾当成障碍。图中可辨识物件：轮椅、平缓的坡道、自动门按钮。

senses.title: Plain lack of capacity
senses.definition: the state of being unable to do something
senses.definitionCN: （名词）做不到某事的状态

intro.en: Disability is dis- not plus ability, which comes through Old French able from Latin habilis, handy, from habere, to have or hold.
intro.cn: disability 是 dis-（不）加 ability；ability 经古法语 able 来自拉丁语 habilis（顺手的），habilis 又来自 habere（拥有、握住）。

items.en: Habere meant to have or hold.
items.cn: habere 意为拥有、握住。

items.en: Habilis meant handy or fit.
items.cn: habilis 意为顺手的、合适的。

items.en: Old French able meant capable.
items.cn: 古法语 able 意为有能力的。

items.en: Ability entered English for capacity.
items.cn: 十五世纪 ability 以「能力」义进入英语。

items.en: Dis- turned it into lack of capacity.
items.cn: 十六世纪 dis- 把它变成能力的缺失。

items.en: The word became central to access and rights.
items.cn: 二十世纪这个词成为无障碍与权利议题的核心。

definition_zh: 应对；应付；处理；承受；勉强维持
definition_en: to deal with a difficulty, a load or a demand using the resources one has
core_image: 一个人顶着风把伞撑开，伞骨被吹得反折，他没有松手，而是侧过身换了个角度继续往前走
scene: 急诊走廊里，护士推着车穿过人群，墙上的排班表被临时改写了好几处。 The night team must cope with twice the usual number of arrivals.
sceneCN: 这里指承受并处理超出平常的工作量（第 2 个义项：应付繁重的任务或需求）；句意为夜班团队必须应对两倍于平常的接诊人数。图中可辨识物件：急诊推车、改写过的排班表、候诊椅、走廊指示牌。

pos.zh: 应对；应付（不及物动词短语加介词，后接困难、压力或任务）
承受；勉强维持（后接负荷、开支或局面）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加动名词词尾构成，义为「应对方式；应对的」
去掉介词后的核心动词，义为「应付；对付」
核心动词的过去式与过去分词形式
