senses.title: Handle pressure
senses.definition: to keep functioning under strain without breaking down
senses.definitionCN: 在压力下仍能运转而不垮掉
senses.example: Students must cope with the strain of three examinations in one week.
senses.exampleCN: 学生必须应对一周三场考试带来的压力。
senses.why: The verb came from a word for exchanging blows; coping is holding one's ground in a contest, not winning it.
senses.whyCN: 核心动词出自表示「交手、对打」的词；应对就是在较量中站住，而不是取胜。

senses.title: Manage a heavy workload
senses.definition: to deal with more work or more demand than is usual
senses.definitionCN: 处理超出平常的工作量或需求
senses.example: The small office can cope with a sudden rise in applications.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小办事处能够应付申请量的突然上升。
senses.why: Coping is holding one's ground when the work arrives faster than usual.
senses.whyCN: 当工作来得比平常更快，撑住就是应对。

senses.title: Respond to a crisis
senses.definition: to act effectively when an emergency breaks
senses.definitionCN: 紧急状况发生时能有效行动
senses.example: The hospital may cope with a flood of casualties only if extra staff arrive.
senses.exampleCN: 只有增援人员到达，医院才可能应对大量伤员涌入。
senses.why: A crisis is a blow one meets with whatever hands are free.
senses.whyCN: 危机是用手里现有的人手迎上的一击。

senses.title: Adapt to change
senses.definition: to adjust one's methods to a new condition
senses.definitionCN: 调整做法以适应新的条件
senses.example: Older workers should cope with new software if the training is patient.
senses.exampleCN: 如果培训足够耐心，年长的员工应能适应新软件。
senses.why: Coping with change is turning sideways rather than letting go of the umbrella.
senses.whyCN: 应对变化，是侧过身，而不是松手丢伞。

senses.title: Live with illness or disability
senses.definition: to carry on daily life while managing a long-term condition
senses.definitionCN: 在长期病痛或残障下维持日常生活
senses.example: Families may cope with a long illness by sharing the care.
senses.exampleCN: 家庭可以通过分担照护来应对长期的病痛。
senses.why: A long illness is a long contest, and sharing the care is how a family keeps standing.
senses.whyCN: 长期病痛是一场长久的交手，分担照护是家庭继续站住的方式。

senses.title: Get by on limited money
senses.definition: to manage daily needs with very little income
senses.definitionCN: 以很少的收入维持日常所需
senses.example: A family can cope with a small budget if housing costs stay low.
senses.exampleCN: 如果住房开支不高，一个家庭可以靠小笔预算维持。
senses.why: A small budget is a load one carries by leaving things out, not by winning.
senses.whyCN: 小预算是一副靠舍弃来承担的担子，而不是靠取胜。

senses.title: Bear a mechanical load
senses.definition: to carry a physical load without failing
senses.definitionCN: 承受物理负荷而不失效
senses.example: The old dam must cope with the weight of water after heavy snow.
senses.exampleCN: 大雪之后，这座旧坝必须承受水的重量。
senses.why: The everyday sense of managing a burden extends naturally to structures that must hold under load.
senses.whyCN: 日常「承担重负」的意思，自然延伸到必须承压的结构上。

senses.title: Balance competing demands
senses.definition: to keep several parties satisfied enough to proceed
senses.definitionCN: 使多方各自得到起码的满足以便推进
senses.example: A chair must cope with members who want opposite things.
senses.exampleCN: 主持人必须应付想要相反结果的成员。
senses.why: A chair meets opposite demands by standing between them rather than over them.
senses.whyCN: 主持人站在相反诉求之间，而不是压在其上。

senses.title: Endure an emotional loss
senses.definition: to continue living after a loss without being overwhelmed
senses.definitionCN: 在失去之后继续生活而不被压垮
senses.example: Children may cope with grief better when routines are kept.
senses.exampleCN: 若日常节律得以保持，孩子可能更好地承受悲伤。
senses.why: Grief is a blow that cannot be avoided, only stood through.
senses.whyCN: 悲伤是一击无法躲开，只能撑过去。

intro.en: The phrase joins a verb that once meant to strike or to trade blows with a preposition of accompaniment. Coping is meeting a difficulty head on and continuing to stand.
intro.cn: 这个短语把曾经表示「打击、交手」的动词与表示「与、同」的介词结合起来。所谓应对，就是正面遇上困难，并且继续站住。

items.en: Kolaphos meant a blow or a cuff, especially one given with the fist.
items.cn: 这个词意为「一击、一巴掌」，尤指用拳头打。

items.en: Latin borrowed the word as colaphus, still naming a blow.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个词，仍然表示「一击」。

items.en: French shortened it to coup, a stroke or a blow, and built the verb couper, to strike.
items.cn: 法语把它缩短为「一击、一记」，并造出「打击」的动词。

items.en: English took the verb for meeting an opponent in combat, and only later for meeting any difficulty.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪引入这个动词，指在战斗中迎击对手，后来才指迎接任何困难。

items.en: The frame with the preposition of accompaniment fixed in the nineteenth century for managing burdens, loads and losses. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 与伴随介词搭配的框架在十九世纪固定下来，用于应对负担、负荷与丧失。最早书证年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the blow word or looks close to it; the second group holds other verbs for dealing with a difficulty.
note.cn: 第一组共享「打击」之词或形近；第二组是其他表示「处理困难」的动词。

entries.definition: Used alone, it means to manage or to get by; the preposition is what brings the specific difficulty into the sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 单独使用时意为「应付、过得去」；正是介词把具体的困难带进句子。

entries.definition: It names the way a person manages, as in a coping strategy; the phrase names the encounter itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词指一个人应对的方式，如应对策略；短语指遭遇本身。

entries.definition: It still means a stroke or a sudden seizure of power; it shares the blow word but not the sense of endurance.
entries.definitionCN: 仍指「一击」或「突然夺取政权」；共享「打击」之词，却不含「撑住」之意。

entries.definition: It comes from a Latin word for abundance, not from the blow word; the resemblance is only in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 它出自拉丁语表示「充裕」的词，与「打击」之词无关，相似只在拼写。

entries.definition: The common phrase for taking action on a problem; it says nothing about whether one has enough resources.
entries.definitionCN: 处理问题的常用短语，不涉及是否有足够资源。

entries.definition: It stresses skill in managing a situation, often with a lighter tone than the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 强调处理局面的技巧，语气常比本短语轻松。

entries.definition: It stresses lasting through pain without any implication of managing the cause.
entries.definitionCN: 强调在痛苦中撑过去，不含「处理成因」之意。

entries.definition: It suggests close, difficult struggle with a problem, and is more vivid than the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 暗示与问题近身缠斗，比本短语更形象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the umbrella in the wind, the rewritten rota, the dam after snow and the shared care.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用风中的伞、改写的排班表、雪后的坝与分担的照护四个场景。

normal.en: An umbrella bent backward by wind, held on and turned sideways.
normal.cn: 伞被风吹得反折，人没有松手，只是侧过身。

normal.en: A rota rewritten three times in one night.
normal.cn: 一张排班表，一夜之间改了三次。

normal.en: An old dam holding back meltwater after a heavy snow.
normal.cn: 大雪之后，旧坝拦住融水。

normal.en: Two sisters sharing the care of an ill parent.
normal.cn: 两姐妹分担照护生病的母亲。

normal.en: A child whose bedtime stays the same through a family upheaval.
normal.cn: 家里天翻地覆，孩子的睡觉时间却没变。

abstract.en: Coping is not solving: it is continuing while the problem continues.
abstract.cn: 应对不是解决：问题还在，人还在往前走。

abstract.en: The word began as trading blows, and it still carries the stance of a fighter who has not fallen.
abstract.cn: 这个词最初指交手，至今仍带着「没有倒下」的姿态。

abstract.en: Resources decide what coping looks like: the same difficulty needs a different answer in a rich room and a poor one.
abstract.cn: 资源决定应对的模样：同一个困难，在富裕的屋里与拮据的屋里需要不同答案。

examples.en: Small firms must cope with delays that larger rivals can absorb.
examples.cn: 小公司必须应对大对手能吸收掉的延误。

examples.en: Coastal towns may cope with a rise in sea level only with new defences.
examples.cn: 沿海城镇只有建起新防线，才可能应对海平面上升。

examples.en: A bridge designed for horses must cope with modern truck traffic.
examples.cn: 为马车设计的桥，必须承受现代卡车的通行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「寇普 威兹」：把「交手」记成顶着风撑伞不肯松手——风还在，人还站着，这就是应对

root: 核心动词出自希腊语表示「一击、一拳」的词，经拉丁语与古法语进入英语，本义是「打击、交手」，后引申为「迎上困难并撑住」。介词为本族常用词，意为「与、同」。短语整体强调用现有资源继续对付，而不保证解决。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses meet a load and keep going: pressure, workload, crisis, change, illness, a small budget, a physical load, competing demands, and grief.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都是遇上一个负荷并继续前行：压力、工作量、危机、变化、疾病、小预算、物理负荷、相互冲突的诉求与悲伤。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person holding an umbrella that the wind has bent backward, turning sideways rather than letting go.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人撑着被风吹反的伞，侧过身继续走，而不是松手。

branches.en: THE INNER LOAD: exam strain and grief are carried without visible machinery.
branches.cn: 内在负荷：考试压力与悲伤在没有可见器械的情况下被承住。

branches.en: THE SUDDEN SURGE: an office absorbs extra applications, a hospital absorbs casualties.
branches.cn: 骤增：办事处吸收额外申请，医院吸收大量伤员。

branches.en: THE ADJUSTED STANCE: new software, opposite demands, a chair turning sideways.
branches.cn: 调整姿态：新软件、相反诉求，主持人侧身应对。

branches.en: THE LONG HAUL: shared care and a tight budget are managed day after day.
branches.cn: 长期支撑：分担照护与紧张预算，一天一天地维持。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL LOAD: a dam or a bridge must hold under weight.
branches.cn: 物理负荷：坝或桥必须在重量下撑住。

intro.en: The family is small and verbal; it grew from a word for a blow, and the endings name the manner and the person rather than a Latin technical vocabulary.
intro.cn: 这个词族人少且以动词为主；它从表示「一击」的词长成，词尾命名方式与人，而不是拉丁技术词汇。

latinIntro.en: Greek and Latin both supplied the blow word, French reshaped it, and English added its own endings.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语与拉丁语都提供了「打击」之词，法语加以改写，英语再加上自己的词尾。

items.example: The oldest word in the family.

senses.title: Noun class in grammar
senses.definition: one of the classes into which a language sorts nouns, often marked masculine, feminine or neuter
senses.definitionCN: 语言为名词划分的类别之一，常标为阳性、阴性或中性
senses.example: In French, gender decides whether the article is le or la.
senses.exampleCN: 在法语中，语法性别决定冠词用 le 还是 la。
senses.why: the word began as a grammar term: nouns were grouped by kind, and the groups were called genders.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是语法术语：名词按类别分组，这些组就叫语法性别。

senses.title: Socially constructed role expectations
senses.definition: the behaviour, duties and expectations a society attaches to being a man or a woman
senses.definitionCN: 社会加诸身为男性或女性的行为、职责与期待
senses.example: The study asks how gender shapes who is expected to cook at home.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究追问性别如何塑造「谁该在家做饭」的期待。
senses.why: twentieth-century scholarship separated this social layer from the older grammar term and made it the dominant sense.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪学术把这一社会层面与旧的语法术语分开，并使它成为主导义。

senses.title: Biological classification
senses.definition: the grouping of organisms as male or female by reproductive anatomy and function
senses.definitionCN: 按生殖解剖结构与功能把生物分为雄性、雌性
senses.example: Some fish change gender as they mature.
senses.exampleCN: 有些鱼在成熟过程中会改变生理性别。
senses.why: biology borrowed the word for the reproductive categories themselves, apart from social roles.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用这个词来指生殖类别本身，与社会角色无关。

senses.title: A person's felt identity
senses.definition: the sense a person has of being male, female or another category, whether or not it matches birth records
senses.definitionCN: 个人对自身属于男性、女性或其他类别的感受，无论是否与出生记录一致
senses.example: The clinic lets patients describe their gender in their own words.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所让就诊者用自己的话描述性别认同。
senses.why: if gender is a role, then who one is as gendered cannot be read off the body alone.
senses.whyCN: 如果性别是一种角色，那么一个人作为性别主体的身份就不能只从身体读出。

senses.title: Analytical category in social science
senses.titleCN: 社会科学中的分析范畴
senses.definition: a category used to compare how resources, labour and power are distributed between men and women
senses.definitionCN: 用于比较资源、劳动与权力在男女之间如何分配的范畴
senses.example: Gender is a standard variable in studies of wages and care work.
senses.exampleCN: 在研究工资与照护劳动时，性别是一个标准变量。
senses.why: once separated from grammar, the word became a tool for measuring unequal arrangements.
senses.whyCN: 一旦与语法分开，这个词就成了衡量不平等安排的工具。

senses.title: Gender forms inside language
senses.definition: the distinctions a language makes in pronouns, agreement and titles to mark male or female reference
senses.definitionCN: 语言在代词、一致关系与称谓上为标示男性或女性所指而作出的区分
senses.example: English marks gender in pronouns but barely in nouns.
senses.exampleCN: 英语在代词上标出性别，在名词上却几乎没有。
senses.why: this sense returns to grammar but focuses on forms rather than on noun classes.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项回到语法，却聚焦于形式而非名词类别。

senses.title: Kind or sort, the old sense
senses.definition: a kind or sort of thing, the sense the word carried when it first entered English
senses.definitionCN: 事物的种类或类别，这是该词初入英语时携带的含义
senses.example: The archaic phrase all genders of goods meant every kind of merchandise.
senses.exampleCN: 古语短语「商品的所有种类」意为各类商品。
senses.why: the oldest English sense is simply kind, which is what Latin genus meant.
senses.whyCN: 英语中最早的义项就是种类，也就是拉丁 genus 的意思。

senses.title: A dimension in policy
senses.definition: a formal axis used to check whether rules, budgets or services affect men and women differently
senses.definitionCN: 用来检查规则、预算或服务是否对男女产生不同影响的正式维度
senses.example: Every budget line is reviewed for its gender impact.
senses.exampleCN: 每条预算项目都要审查其性别影响。
senses.why: governments turned the analytical category into an administrative checkpoint.
senses.whyCN: 政府把这一分析范畴变成了行政审查环节。

intro.en: Gender comes from Old French gendre, from Latin genus, generis 'kind, race, stock'. It entered English first as a grammar term, and the biological and social senses are twentieth-century developments. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: gender 来自古法语 gendre，源于拉丁 genus、generis「种类、族类」。它初入英语时是语法术语，生理与社会义都是二十世纪的演变。年代均为约数。

items.en: genus meant 'kind, race, stock, family'. Its deeper origin is source uncertain; the older root sometimes cited for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: genus 意为「种类、族类、血统、家族」。其更深来源不确定；有人为它引用的更早词根属于重构形式。

items.en: generis is the genitive singular of genus; the stem gener- is the form that passed through French into English.
items.cn: generis 是 genus 的单数属格；进入法语再进入英语的正是 gener- 这个词干。

items.en: Old French gendre meant 'kind' and also named the grammatical classes of nouns; Middle English borrowed it as gendre.
items.cn: 古法语 gendre 意为「种类」，也指名词的语法类别；中古英语把它借入为 gendre。

items.en: From the fourteenth century the word was used for the masculine, feminine and neuter classes of nouns, and this remained its main sense for centuries.
items.cn: 从十四世纪起，这个词用于名词的阳性、阴性与中性类别，此后数百年间这都是它的主要义项。

items.en: The plain sense 'kind or sort' stayed in use alongside the grammar sense and is now archaic in everyday speech.
items.cn: 「种类、类别」这一朴素义与语法义长期并存，如今在日常语言中已属古旧。

items.en: The biological sense is a twentieth-century extension, and the social sense is generally thought to have spread through mid-twentieth-century psychology and sociology.
items.cn: 生理义是二十世纪的扩展；一般认为社会义经二十世纪中期心理学与社会学传播开来。

note.en: Group one holds words that look close to gender but come from a different Greek or Latin branch; group two holds terms for sex and desire that are often confused with it.
note.cn: 第一组是与 gender 形近、却出自不同希腊或拉丁分支的词；第二组是常与它混淆的性、欲望相关词。

entries.definition: Coined in the early twentieth century from Greek genos 'birth, race', not from Latin genus: a unit of heredity, with no grammatical or social meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 二十世纪初据希腊 genos「出生、族类」造出，而非来自拉丁 genus：指遗传单位，没有语法或社会含义。

entries.definition: The Latin noun itself, used in biology for a rank above species; it is the direct source of gender, but it names a taxonomic class rather than a person's identity.
entries.definitionCN: 就是那个拉丁名词，生物学中用作高于物种的等级；它是 gender 的直接来源，却指分类层级，而非个人身份。

entries.definition: A French branch of the same Latin genus: a category of art or writing. It is a cousin of gender, not a synonym, and carries no idea of sex.
entries.definitionCN: 同一拉丁 genus 的法语分支：指艺术或写作的类别。它是 gender 的表亲而非同义词，不含性别之意。

entries.definition: Latin gener- plus -ic: belonging to a whole class rather than a specific member, as in a generic drug or a generic label.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁 gener- 加 -ic：属于整个类别而非特定成员，如通用药物或通用标签。

entries.definition: The biological categories of male and female, or sexual activity; gender is the social and identity layer that may or may not match it.
entries.definitionCN: 指雄雌的生理类别，或性行为；gender 是可能与之相符也可能不符的社会与认同层面。

entries.definition: A person's sexual orientation and capacity for attraction; it concerns desire, not the rank or role that gender names.
entries.definitionCN: 指个人的性取向与产生吸引的能力；它关乎欲望，而非 gender 所指的位次或角色。

entries.definition: The direction of sexual or romantic attraction; a narrower term than gender and not a category of identity in the same sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指性方面或情感方面受吸引的方向；比 gender 窄，也不是同一意义上的身份类别。

entries.definition: Prejudice or discrimination based on sex; it names a practice, while gender names the category that the practice polices.
entries.definitionCN: 基于生理性别的偏见或歧视；它命名一种做法，而 gender 命名这种做法所规训的类别。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin genus 'kind' became French gendre: a class, first of nouns, later of people.
normal.cn: 拉丁 genus「种类」变成法语 gendre：先是名词的类别，后来是人的类别。

normal.en: The family runs gendered, gendering, genderless, misgender, gender-neutral.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 gendered、gendering、genderless、misgender、gender-neutral。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark public debate: gender equality, gender roles, gender gap.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出公共议题：性别平等、性别角色、性别差距。

normal.en: Grammar is the oldest layer: French nouns take le or la by gender.
normal.cn: 语法是最早的层面：法语名词按语法性别取 le 或 la。

normal.en: The social sense is recent, roughly mid-twentieth century, not medieval.
normal.cn: 社会义出现得晚，大约在二十世纪中期，并非中世纪产物。

abstract.en: Picture two identical boxes given different coloured labels by the person holding the pen.
abstract.cn: 想象两个一模一样的盒子，标签颜色由拿笔的人决定。

abstract.en: Picture a noun waiting at a counter to be told which line it belongs to.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名词在柜台前等着被告知属于哪一队。

abstract.cn: 想象一张表格，只有一个空格，每个人用自己的笔迹填写。

examples.en: The report measures the gender gap in promotions rather than in hiring.
examples.cn: 这份报告衡量的是晋升中的性别差距，而非招聘中的差距。

examples.en: Latin has three genders, and some languages have none.
examples.cn: 拉丁语有三个语法性别，有些语言则一个也没有。

examples.en: The policy treats gender as a budget dimension, not a private matter.
examples.cn: 该政策把性别当作预算维度，而非私事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「gen（种类）+ der」——先给名词分种类，再给人分种类 → 语法性别、社会性别

root: 古法语 gendre < 拉丁 genus、generis「种类、族类」；原为语法术语，指名词的语法性别；生理与社会义为 20 世纪演变；genus 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one move, sorting into kinds: nouns are sorted by grammar, people by social expectation, bodies by biology, selves by identity, data by analysis, language by forms, old texts by the plain sense of kind, and budgets by policy.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开，即分门别类：名词按语法分，人按社会期待分，身体按生理分，自我按认同分，数据按分析分，语言按形式分，古文本按「种类」的朴素义分，预算按政策分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: labels stuck onto boxes of the same shape, the colour chosen by the hand holding the label.
core.cn: 核心意象：标签贴在形状相同的盒子上，颜色由拿标签的那只手选定。

branches.en: GRAMMAR TWICE: first the class of a noun, later the forms pronouns and titles use to mark it.
branches.cn: 两次回到语法：先指名词的类别，后指代词与称谓用来标示它的一整套形式。

branches.en: ROLE AND BODY: one reading is what society expects, the other what anatomy records.
branches.cn: 角色与身体：一种读法是社会的期待，另一种读法是解剖的记录。

branches.en: SELF AND DATA: identity is felt from inside, while the analytical category is counted from outside.
branches.cn: 自我与数据：认同从内部感受，分析范畴则从外部计数。

branches.en: OLD KIND: strip away sex and grammar, and the word still means a sort of thing.
branches.cn: 古老的种类义：抽去性与语法，这个词仍然只指一类事物。

branches.en: POLICY AXIS: the category becomes a checkpoint applied to every budget line.
branches.cn: 政策轴线：这个范畴变成适用于每条预算项目的审查关卡。

intro.en: Gender is a Latin noun that came through French with almost no suffix of its own, so its family is built by adding English endings to the bare stem.
intro.cn: gender 是经法语传来的拉丁名词，本身几乎没有后缀，因此它的词族靠在裸词干上加英语词尾来构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin genus, generis gives the stem gener-, seen in generare and generatio; English gender, gendered, gendering, genderless and misgender all grow from that stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 genus、generis 提供 gener- 词干，见于 generare 与 generatio；英语 gender、gendered、gendering、genderless 与 misgender 都从这个词干长出。

items.example: The noun names a class of things sharing a origin.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指共享同一来源的一类事物。

items.meaning: of a kind, of a race
items.example: The genitive form supplies the stem gener- for the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个属格形式为整个词族提供了 gener- 词干。

definition_zh: 领地行为；动物划定、标记并守卫一片专属区域的行为
definition_en: the behavior by which an animal claims a particular area, marks its boundary and keeps other individuals out
core_image: 一只鸟每天停在树篱的同一根枝条上鸣叫，把整片灌木丛划成自己的地盘
scene: 清晨的树篱边，一只雄鸟反复停在同一个枝头高声鸣唱，把这片灌木丛当成自己的地盘。 A male songbird returns to the same twig each dawn and sings, a pattern that biologists record as territorial behavior.
sceneCN: 这里 territorial behavior 指「动物划定并守卫专属区域的行为」（第 1 个义项：用固定边界把同类排除在外）；句意为一只雄鸟每天清晨回到同一根枝条鸣唱，生物学家把这种规律性举动记录为领地行为。图中可辨识物件：树篱、同一根枝条、鸣唱的雄鸟、靠近的同类、看不见的边界线。

pos.zh: 领地行为（动物对一片区域的占有、标记与防卫；作不可数名词，指具体类型时可有复数）

derivatives.zh: 领地性；对空间的排他性占有倾向
把某片区域划为领地；使领地化

senses.title: Claim and hold an exclusive area
senses.definition: to claim a particular area as one's own and keep other individuals out of it
senses.definitionCN: 把某片区域认作自己的地盘，并把其他个体排除在外
senses.example: The pair defends the same stretch of bank from spring to autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 这一对鸟从春天到秋天守着同一段河岸。
senses.why: territorial draws a boundary around land, and behavior supplies the acts that enforce it; together they name the whole claim-and-exclude pattern.
senses.whyCN: territorial 划出土地的边界，behavior 提供执行边界的动作；合起来命名「宣称并排除」的整套模式。

senses.title: Drive intruders away
senses.definition: to chase or attack individuals that enter the claimed area
senses.definitionCN: 追赶或攻击进入所占地盘的同类个体
senses.example: The male chases every rival that crosses the hedge.
senses.exampleCN: 雄鸟会追赶每一只越过树篱的对手。
senses.why: once a line is drawn, enforcement is the visible part of the behavior: pursuit, threat and contact are how the boundary is made real.
senses.whyCN: 边界一旦划出，执法就是行为中看得见的部分：追击、威胁与身体接触让这条边界真正成立。

senses.title: Mark the boundary by signals
senses.titleCN: 用鸣唱、气味或视觉标记标出边界
senses.definition: to advertise ownership through song, scent, calls or visual displays
senses.definitionCN: 用鸣唱、气味、叫声或视觉展示宣告占有
senses.example: The warbler sings from the same post every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 这只莺每天清晨在同一根木桩上鸣唱。
senses.why: a boundary is invisible unless it is broadcast, so marking is the cheap alternative to fighting: the signal says the owner is present and ready.
senses.whyCN: 边界本身看不见，必须被广播出去；标记因此是打斗之外的低成本手段——信号说明主人就在附近且随时应战。

senses.title: Defend food, nests and mates
senses.titleCN: 守住食物、巢址与配偶等资源
senses.definition: to protect the resources inside an area from being used by others
senses.definitionCN: 保护区域内的资源不被其他个体使用
senses.example: Each pair keeps the insects near its nest for its own chicks.
senses.exampleCN: 每一对鸟都把巢边的昆虫留给自己的雏鸟。
senses.why: territory is usually worth defending because it contains something scarce; the area is a container, and the resource is the reason for the container.
senses.whyCN: 领地之所以值得守卫，通常因为其中装着稀缺资源；区域是容器，资源才是容器存在的理由。

senses.title: Seasonal territory in the breeding season
senses.titleCN: 繁殖季出现的临时领地
senses.definition: a territory held only for part of the year, typically while breeding
senses.definitionCN: 只在一年中某段时间、通常繁殖期才占有的领地
senses.example: The males arrive in April, claim a reed patch, and leave in July.
senses.exampleCN: 雄鸟四月到达，占下一片芦苇，七月离开。
senses.why: when the young are reared and gone, the reason for the boundary disappears with them, so the territory can be given up without loss.
senses.whyCN: 雏鸟养大离巢后，边界存在的理由也随之消失，因此领地可以毫无损失地放弃。

senses.title: Space individuals apart
senses.titleCN: 把同类个体在空间上隔开
senses.definition: a spacing mechanism that keeps members of a population at a distance from one another
senses.definitionCN: 一种把种群成员相互隔开的间距调节机制
senses.example: Density falls because singing males keep their neighbours at a distance.
senses.exampleCN: 鸣唱的雄鸟让邻居保持距离，密度因此下降。
senses.why: seen from the population level, the same boundary works like a valve: it limits how many individuals can settle in one place.
senses.whyCN: 从种群层面看，同一条边界像一道阀门：它限制了多少个体能在同一处落脚。

senses.title: Applied to human space
senses.titleCN: 借用于人对空间与座位的占有
senses.definition: the human tendency to claim a seat, desk or corner and resent intrusion
senses.definitionCN: 人占据座位、书桌或角落并反感他人侵入的倾向
senses.example: Office workers show territorial behavior over their desks.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室职员对自己的书桌表现出领地行为。
senses.why: the word moved from animals to people because the same geometry appears in offices: a marked spot, a habitual user stream, and a sense of trespass.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从动物扩展到人，是因为办公室里出现同样的几何关系：被标记的位置、惯常使用者，以及被侵犯的感觉。

senses.title: A measurable category in field studies
senses.titleCN: 野外研究中可观察、可计数的行为类别
senses.definition: a recorded class of actions such as patrols, songs and chases used in behavioral research
senses.definitionCN: 行为研究中记录的一类动作，如巡逻、鸣唱与追赶
senses.example: The observer logs every chase as one bout of territorial behavior.
senses.exampleCN: 观察者把每一次追赶记为一次领地行为。
senses.why: science needs countable units; naming the whole pattern lets a field worker turn scattered actions into a column of numbers.
senses.whyCN: 科学需要可计数的单位；给整套模式命名，野外工作者才能把零散动作变成一列数字。

intro.en: Territorial comes from Latin terra 'earth' through territorium, while behavior is a native English formation from be- plus have. The full phrase is a twentieth-century ethological term. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: territorial 经 territorium 源自拉丁 terra「土地」；behavior 是英语本土构造，由 be- 加 have 构成。整个短语是 20 世纪的动物行为学术语。年代为约数。

items.en: Terra meant 'earth, dry land'; from it Latin built territorium, the land lying around a town and subject to its control.
items.cn: terra 意为「土地、干地」；拉丁语由此构成 territorium，指城邦周边受其控制的土地。

items.en: Late Latin territorialis 'of a territory' passed through French and entered English as territorial in the early seventeenth century.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 territorialis 意为「领地所属的」，经法语进入英语，17 世纪初形成 territorial。

items.era: OLD ENGLISH AND MIDDLE ENGLISH BEHAVE
items.en: Behavior derives from behave, formed in Middle English from be- plus have (Old English habban 'to hold'); to behave is literally to hold or bear oneself in a certain way.
items.cn: behavior 来自 behave；behave 是中古英语由 be- 加 have（古英语 habban「持有」）构成，字面义是「以某种方式持住自己」。

items.en: Territorial behavior became a standard label in animal behavior studies in the early twentieth century, when field workers began mapping areas that birds and mammals defend.
items.cn: 20 世纪初，野外研究者开始绘制鸟类与哺乳动物防卫的区域，territorial behavior 由此成为动物行为学的标准说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest use of the exact phrase territorial behavior is not precisely recorded, and the boundary between territory and home range is defined differently across schools.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：territorial behavior 这一确切短语的最早书证没有精确记录；不同学派对「领地」与「活动范围」的界线定义也不一致。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same territorial family that are easily swapped; group two holds spatial and behavioral terms with overlapping meanings.
note.cn: 第一组是同一 territorial 词族里容易被混用的形式；第二组是含义有重叠的空间与行为术语。

entries.definition: The tendency or system of holding and defending a territory; it names the principle, not the observable acts.
entries.definitionCN: 占有并防卫领地的倾向或制度；指原则本身，而非可观察的动作。

entries.definition: The area itself that is claimed; territory can exist on a map even when no animal is currently patrolling it.
entries.definitionCN: 被宣称占有的那块地方；即使当下没有动物巡逻，领地在图上仍可存在。

entries.definition: Pertaining to a territory; it needs a noun such as behavior, waters or dispute to complete it.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「领地的」；必须搭配 behavior、waters 或 dispute 之类名词才完整。

entries.definition: A belt of sea under a state's jurisdiction; the same adjective, but the boundary is legal rather than behavioral.
entries.definitionCN: 受国家管辖的近海带；形容词相同，但边界是法律划定的，不是行为划出的。

entries.definition: The area an animal routinely uses for feeding and shelter; unlike a territory, it is not actively defended against all rivals.
entries.definitionCN: 动物日常觅食与栖居所用的区域；与领地不同，它并不主动排除所有同类。

entries.definition: Actions that establish rank within a group; dominance is about who yields, territory is about where others may not go.
entries.definitionCN: 在群体中确立等级的动作；dominance 关乎谁让步，territory 关乎别人不能去哪里。

entries.definition: Attacking or threatening; it is one tool of territorial defense, not the whole pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 攻击或威胁；它只是领地防卫的一种手段，并不等于整套模式。

entries.definition: Any behavior that regulates distance between individuals; territorial defense is one form of it.
entries.definitionCN: 任何调节个体间距的行为；领地防卫是其中一种形式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: terra 'land' gives territorium 'land around a town', then territorial 'of a territory'; add behavior and you have the acts that hold that land.
normal.cn: terra「土地」构成 territorium「城郊土地」，再形成 territorial「领地的」；加上 behavior，就是守住那片土地的动作。

normal.en: The family runs territory, territorial, territoriality, territorialize and behavior.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 territory、territorial、territoriality、territorialize 与 behavior。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the core: defend a territory, mark a boundary, drive off intruders, hold a home range.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出核心：守卫领地、标出边界、赶走入侵者、占据活动范围。

normal.en: A territory is defended; a home range is merely used. The pair of terms is a standard exam distinction.
normal.cn: 领地要被守卫，活动范围只是被使用；这一对术语是常见的考试区分点。

normal.en: The adjective territorial is almost always followed by a noun, so the phrase itself is the unit to memorize.
normal.cn: 形容词 territorial 后面几乎总要跟名词，因此要记的单位正是整个短语。

abstract.en: Picture a fence drawn in scent rather than wire, invisible to us but sharp to a dog.
abstract.cn: 想象一道用气味而不是铁丝画出的篱笆，人看不见，狗却分得清。

abstract.en: Picture a singer returning to the same post every dawn, not for the song but for the line it draws.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鸟每天清晨回到同一根木桩，不为唱歌，而为歌声划出的那条线。

abstract.en: Picture a crowded beach where every group leaves one empty towel-width between itself and the next.
abstract.cn: 想象拥挤的海滩上，每一群人都与邻座留出一条毛巾宽的空隙。

examples.en: Wolves scent-mark the pack's boundary throughout the year.
examples.cn: 狼群全年都在用气味标记群体的边界。

examples.en: Bluebirds defend a nest box against other pairs of the same species.
examples.cn: 蓝鸲会守卫巢箱，不让同种的其他配对进入。

examples.en: The term territorial behavior appears in almost every field guide to animal behavior.
examples.cn: 几乎所有动物行为野外指南都会出现 territorial behavior 这一术语。

dict_mnemonic.text: territory（地盘）+ behavior（行为）——把一片地划成自己的，再守住它 → 领地行为

root: territorial 源自拉丁 terra「土地」，经 territorium「城郊土地」；behavior 源自中古英语 behaven，由 be- 加古英语 habban「持有」构成。合指「守住一片土地的行为」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one loop: a boundary is claimed, broadcast, enforced, and then read either as a resource defence, a seasonal arrangement, a spacing valve, a human habit or a research unit.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个循环展开：先宣称边界，再广播边界、执行边界，随后可读作资源防卫、季节性安排、间距阀门、人类习惯或研究单位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line around land, drawn once and then kept by signal and chase.
core.cn: 核心意象：绕着一片土地画一条线，画定之后靠信号与追赶维持。

branches.en: CLAIM AND ENFORCE: the claim exists only while it is backed by pursuit.
branches.cn: 宣称与执行：宣称只有在追赶的支撑下才存在。

branches.en: BROADCAST: song and scent make the invisible line public.
branches.cn: 广播：鸣唱与气味把看不见的线变成公开信息。

branches.en: WHY HOLD IT: scarce food and a seasonal nest are the reasons a line is worth defending.
branches.cn: 为何守住：稀缺食物与季节性巢址，是这条线值得守的理由。

branches.en: POPULATION VALVE: many private lines together set the distance between all individuals.
branches.cn: 种群阀门：许多条私人界线合起来，决定了所有个体之间的间距。

branches.en: TRANSFER: the same geometry appears in an office desk and in a researcher's tally sheet.
branches.cn: 迁移：同样的几何关系出现在办公桌与研究者的记录表上。

intro.en: Territorial behavior joins a Latin land-word to an English manner-word; each half keeps its own family, so the phrase is best read in two parts.
intro.cn: territorial behavior 把一个拉丁土地词与一个英语方式词连在一起；两半各自保留词族，因此最好分两部分读。

latinIntro.en: Latin terra 'earth' yields territorium and territorialis; the English adjective territorial and the noun territoriality continue that line. Behavior has no Latin cognate and comes from Germanic have.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 terra「土地」衍生 territorium 与 territorialis；英语形容词 territorial 与名词 territoriality 延续这条线。behavior 没有拉丁同族词，来自日耳曼语的 have。

items.example: Terra is the base of territory and terrestrial.
items.exampleCN: terra 是 territory 与 terrestrial 的基础。

items.meaning: land around a town, a district under control
items.meaningCN: 城郊土地；受管辖的区域
items.example: The Roman district gave its name to every later territory.
items.exampleCN: 罗马的辖区把名字留给了后世每一种 territory。

items.example: The Late Latin adjective passed into French and English.
items.exampleCN: 这个晚期拉丁形容词经法语进入英语。

items.meaning: of or relating to a territory
items.example: Territorial claims are marked on the map.
items.exampleCN: 领地主张被标在地图上。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun of place into an adjective of place.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把表示地点的名词变成表示地点的形容词。

items.example: Territorial plus -ity names the tendency itself.
items.exampleCN: territorial 加 -ity 命名这种倾向本身。

items.meaning: the state of holding and defending a territory
items.meaningCN: 占有并防卫领地的状态
items.example: Territoriality keeps neighbouring pairs apart.
items.exampleCN: 领地性使相邻的配对保持距离。

items.meaning: the way a person or animal acts
items.example: Behavior is what an observer can actually record.
items.exampleCN: 行为是观察者真正能记录下来的东西。

items.meaning: around, thoroughly, or making a verb transitive
items.meaningCN: 围绕、彻底，或使动词及物
items.example: Be- turns have into behave, to hold oneself.
items.exampleCN: be- 把 have 变成 behave，即「持住自己」。

items.example: Behavioral ecology studies these boundary patterns.
items.exampleCN: 行为生态学研究这类边界模式。

latinEntries.meaning: land around a town; a district

definition_zh: 墓碑；墓石；碑文；（数据库中的）删除标记
definition_en: a stone set at a grave to mark it and carry the dead person's name, or, in computing, a marker that records a deleted item
core_image: 一块半埋的灰色石板立在草丛里，上面刻着姓名、两个年份和一行小字，字口里积着尘土
scene: 草丛里立着一块半埋的灰色石板，上面刻着姓名、两个年份和一行小字，字口里积着尘土。 Half sunk in grass, the tombstone still carries a name, two years and a line worn thin by weather.
sceneCN: 这里 tombstone 指「立在墓前、刻有姓名与年份以标记墓位的石板」（第 1 个义项：作为墓位标识的立石）；句意为草丛中的石板半埋，上面仍可读出姓名、两个年份与一行被风雨磨薄的字。可辨识物件：石板、刻字、草丛、土堆、苔痕。

pos.zh: 墓碑；墓石
（计算机）删除标记；墓碑记录

senses.title: A stone that marks a grave
senses.definition: a stone placed at a grave to identify the person buried there
senses.definitionCN: 立在墓前以标明所葬之人的石块
senses.example: The tombstone records her name and the year of her death.
senses.exampleCN: 墓碑记着她的姓名与去世年份。
senses.why: Tombstone is a plain compound of tomb and stone: a stone whose job is to mark a tomb and keep a name visible.
senses.whyCN: tombstone 是 tomb 与 stone 的朴素复合：一块以标记墓、让名字保持可见为职责的石头。

senses.title: A flat slab over the grave
senses.titleCN: 墓石：覆盖墓穴的平石板
senses.definition: a flat stone laid horizontally over a grave rather than standing upright
senses.definitionCN: 横铺在墓穴上、而非竖立的石板
senses.example: The tombstone lies flat and has lost its edges.
senses.exampleCN: 这块墓石平铺着，边缘已经磨圆。
senses.why: Not every marker stands; a slab seals the grave as well as labels it, and the same word covers both jobs.
senses.whyCN: 并非所有标记都竖立；石板既封住墓穴又标明它，同一个词涵盖这两项功能。

senses.title: The inscription on the stone
senses.definition: the carved text on a grave stone, including name, dates and a short message
senses.definitionCN: 墓石上刻的文字，含姓名、年代与简短语句
senses.example: The tombstone reads simply that he loved the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 碑文只写着他爱海。
senses.why: Metonymy again: the marker and the message share one word, because the stone exists to carry the words.
senses.whyCN: 又是转喻：标记与文字共用一个词，因为石头存在的目的就是承载文字。

senses.title: A grave marker in a record
senses.titleCN: 墓位标记：登记系统中的标识
senses.definition: the marker or entry that identifies a grave in a cemetery register or on a plan
senses.definitionCN: 在墓地登记册或平面图上标识某个墓穴的标记或条目
senses.example: The plan uses a tombstone symbol for each plot.
senses.exampleCN: 平面图用墓碑符号标出每个墓位。
senses.why: Administration needs symbols, so a small drawn stone can stand for a grave in a register.
senses.whyCN: 管理需要符号，于是一个画出来的小石碑就能在登记册中代表一处墓穴。

senses.title: A mason's carved product
senses.titleCN: 石作成品：石匠制作的碑石
senses.definition: the worked stone as a product of cutting, lettering and finishing
senses.definitionCN: 作为切割、刻字与打磨之成品的加工石
senses.example: The mason delivered the tombstone in two weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 石匠两周后交付了这块墓碑。
senses.why: Looking at the craft, the word names a manufactured object with a trade behind it, not a memorial act.
senses.whyCN: 从工艺角度看，这个词指一件背后有行业支撑的制成品，而不是一次纪念行为。

senses.title: A genealogical marker
senses.titleCN: 族谱标记：家谱研究中的墓石信息
senses.definition: the stone as a source of birth, death, marriage and family data for genealogy
senses.definitionCN: 作为家谱研究中性、婚、死亡与家族数据来源的墓石
senses.example: Genealogists photographed every tombstone in the parish.
senses.exampleCN: 家谱研究者拍下了教区内的每一块墓碑。
senses.why: A stone is also a document: dates and relationships carved in it can be read as records when paper is missing.
senses.whyCN: 石头也是一份文件：纸上记录缺失时，刻在上面的日期与关系可以被当作档案来读。

senses.title: A sign that something has ended
senses.titleCN: 比喻：某事物终结的标志
senses.definition: used figuratively for a visible sign that a project, era or person is finished
senses.definitionCN: 比喻某项目、时代或人物已经结束的可见标志
senses.example: The empty factory is a tombstone for the old industry.
senses.exampleCN: 那座空工厂是旧工业的墓碑。
senses.why: A marker tells later visitors who lies here; applied to an ended enterprise, the image says the same thing about an era.
senses.whyCN: 标记告诉后来者这里躺着谁；用于终结的事业，这个意象对某个时代说了同一件事。

senses.title: A deletion marker in computing
senses.titleCN: 删除标记：数据库与分布式系统中的墓碑记录
senses.definition: a small record that marks an item as deleted so that the deletion can propagate and be respected
senses.definitionCN: 把某项标记为已删除、以便删除状态能传播并被遵守的小记录
senses.example: The tombstone prevents the deleted entry from reappearing.
senses.exampleCN: 这条删除标记防止已删条目重新出现。
senses.why: In distributed systems an absent item cannot be distinguished from an item never seen, so a tombstone is left in its place like a stone over an empty grave.
senses.whyCN: 在分布式系统中，缺失的条目与从未出现的条目无法区分，因此要在原处留一块「墓碑」，如同空墓上的石碑。

intro.en: Tombstone is a native compound of tomb, borrowed from Greek through Latin and French, and stone, from Old English stan. The computing sense is a modern metaphor. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: tombstone 是 tomb 与 stone 构成的本族复合词；tomb 经拉丁与法语借自希腊语，stone 出自古英语 stan。计算机义是现代的比喻延伸。年代均为约数。

items.en: Stan meant stone or rock and continues Proto-Germanic *stainaz; it builds stone, stony, cornerstone and tombstone.
items.cn: stan 意为石头或岩石，延续原始日耳曼语 *stainaz；它构成 stone、stony、cornerstone、tombstone。

items.en: Tomb arrived through Latin tumba and Old French tombe from Greek tymbos, a burial mound, keeping the sense of a marked grave.
items.cn: tomb 经拉丁 tumba 与古法语 tombe 来自希腊 tymbos「坟丘」，保留「有标记的墓」这一义。

items.en: English joined the two words to name the stone that marks a grave, a plain descriptive compound rather than a borrowed phrase.
items.cn: 英语把两个词连起来，指标记墓穴的石头；这是朴素的描述性复合，而非借来的短语。

items.en: In the late twentieth century distributed databases borrowed the image: a deleted record leaves a marker that says an entry once existed here.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期，分布式数据库借用了这个意象：被删除的记录留下一个标记，说明此处曾有条目。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first written use of tombstone is not precisely dated, and the date when the computing sense entered general technical use is also approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定：tombstone 的首次书面使用没有确切年代，计算机义进入一般技术用语的年代也只是约数。

note.en: The first group holds words for the same stone under other names; the second group holds markers and memorial objects.
note.cn: 第一组是同一块石头的其他名称；第二组是标记与纪念物类词。

entries.definition: The common synonym for the stone at a grave; tombstone is slightly older and also has the computing sense.
entries.definitionCN: 墓前石块的常用同义词；tombstone 略古，并且还有计算机义。

entries.definition: Specifically the upright stone at the head of a grave; a tombstone may also lie flat.
entries.definitionCN: 特指立在墓首的竖石；tombstone 也可以是平铺的。

entries.definition: The grave or structure; the stone is only its marker.
entries.definitionCN: 坟墓或构筑；石碑只是它的标记。

entries.definition: A plate bearing text fixed to a wall or monument; it marks rather than covers a grave.
entries.definitionCN: 固定在墙或纪念物上的文字牌；它标记，而不覆盖墓穴。

entries.definition: Anything built or kept to remember the dead; a tombstone is one small form of memorial.
entries.definitionCN: 为纪念死者而建或保存的任何东西；墓碑是纪念物的一种小形式。

entries.definition: The words inscribed on a tomb, not the stone that carries them.
entries.definitionCN: 刻在墓上的文字，而非承载文字的石块。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two native halves, the upright and flat forms, the inscription and the database metaphor.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个本族成分、竖立与平铺两种形式、铭文，以及数据库比喻。

normal.en: tomb plus stone: the word simply says what the object is.
normal.cn: tomb 加 stone：这个词直接说明物件是什么。

normal.en: A tombstone may stand at the head of a grave or lie flat over it.
normal.cn: 墓碑可以立在墓首，也可以平铺在墓上。

normal.en: The stone is also a document: names and dates can be read when paper is lost.
normal.cn: 石头也是文件：纸面记录丢失时，姓名与年代仍可读。

normal.en: Metonymy lets tombstone name the inscription as well as the slab.
normal.cn: 转喻使 tombstone 既指石板，也指碑文。

normal.en: In databases a tombstone is a marker left where a deleted record used to be.
normal.cn: 在数据库中，tombstone 是留在被删记录原处的标记。

abstract.en: Abstractly, a tombstone is information made durable in the hardest available material.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，墓碑是把信息固定在可得的最硬材料上。

abstract.en: It answers one question for strangers: who was here.
abstract.cn: 它为陌生人回答一个问题：这里曾是谁。

abstract.en: The computing sense shows how far the image travels: a deleted record also needs a stone.
abstract.cn: 计算机义显示这个意象走得多远：被删除的记录也需要一块石碑。

examples.en: The tombstone was cleaned so the lettering could be read again.
examples.cn: 墓碑经过清理，字迹又能辨认了。

examples.en: A simple tombstone marks the grave of the unknown sailor.
examples.cn: 一块朴素的墓碑标记着那位无名水手的墓。

examples.en: The system writes a tombstone so that the deletion reaches every copy.
examples.cn: 系统写入一条删除标记，使删除状态传到每一份副本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「tomb（墓）+ stone（石）」——墓前那块刻字的石头 → 墓碑

root: tomb（希腊 tymbos「坟丘」经拉丁 tumba、古法语 tombe）+ 古英语 stan「石头」；字面为「墓前的石头」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one slab: it marks a grave, covers it, carries words, enters registers, comes from a mason, feeds genealogy, stands for an ending and even marks a deleted record.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一块石板展开：它标记墓、覆盖墓、承载文字、进入登记册、出自石匠、供家谱研究、象征终结，甚至标记被删除的记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a weathered slab in grass, its cut letters filled with dust.
core.cn: 核心意象：草丛中一块风化的石板，刻字的凹槽里积着尘土。

branches.en: THE WORKED STONE: craft produces the slab, and placing it turns a product into a marker.
branches.cn: 加工之石：工艺造出石板，安放它则把产品变成标记。

branches.en: THE COVER: a flat slab seals the grave as well as naming it.
branches.cn: 覆盖：平石板既封住墓穴，也命名它。

branches.en: WORDS AND SYMBOLS: the inscription and the register entry both make the stone readable as information.
branches.cn: 文字与符号：铭文与登记条目都让石头可作为信息来读。

branches.en: THE LONG RECORD: genealogy reads dates from the stone, and metaphor reads an ending from it.
branches.cn: 长久的记录：家谱从石上读日期，比喻从石上读终结。

branches.en: THE DIGITAL STONE: a deletion marker repeats the gesture in a system where absence needs a sign.
branches.cn: 数字之石：删除标记在「缺席需要符号」的系统里重演同一动作。

intro.en: Tombstone is a plain two-word compound whose halves are both readable, which makes the word unusually transparent.
intro.cn: tombstone 是朴素的双词复合，两半都可读，因此这个词异常透明。

latinIntro.en: The stone half is native English, from Old English stan; the tomb half reached English through Latin tumba from Greek tymbos. No single Latin verb stands behind the compound.
latinIntro.cn: stone 一半是英语本族词，出自古英语 stan；tomb 一半经拉丁 tumba 来自希腊 tymbos。这个复合词背后没有单一拉丁动词。

items.example: Stan is the source of modern stone.
items.exampleCN: stan 是现代 stone 的来源。

items.structure: stone (English noun, from Old English stan)
items.example: The stone was cut and lettered by hand.
items.exampleCN: 这块石头由手工切割并刻字。

items.structure: tomb (English noun, from Greek tymbos via Latin and French)
items.meaning: a grave or built burial structure
items.example: The tomb lies beneath the slab.
items.exampleCN: 墓就在石板之下。

items.example: The tombstone bears two dates.
items.exampleCN: 墓碑上刻着两个年份。

items.example: Gravestone is the commoner everyday word.
items.exampleCN: gravestone 是更常用的日常说法。

items.meaning: the stone standing at the head of a grave
items.example: The headstone faces east.
items.exampleCN: 这块墓碑朝东。

items.meaning: the first stone of a building
items.example: Cornerstone shows the same stone-building pattern.
items.exampleCN: cornerstone 显示同样的「石+构件」构词模式。

items.example: The stonemason carved the letters.
items.exampleCN: 石匠刻下了这些字母。

definition_zh: 爱争论的；论证性的；说理式的
definition_en: tending to argue or disagree, or concerned with presenting reasoned argument
core_image: 一个人手里举着一列理由，随时准备把对方的话推回去
scene: 写作课上老师要求把观点写成有理由支撑的文章，提醒道： This assignment calls for an argumentative essay.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「以论证方式展开的」（第 3 个义项：写作或言谈以理由支撑主张）；句意为这项作业要求写一篇议论文。

pos.zh: 爱争论的；论证性的；说理式的

derivatives.zh: 好争辩地；以论证方式地

senses.title: Fond of arguing
senses.definition: having a habit of disagreeing and arguing with others, often in a quarrelsome way
senses.definitionCN: 有与他人分歧争吵的习惯，常带好斗意味
senses.example: He gets argumentative when he is tired.
senses.exampleCN: 他累的时候就会变得爱争论。
senses.why: The suffix marks a tendency, and the base is the activity of arguing, so the word describes a person inclined to it.
senses.whyCN: 后缀标记倾向，词基是争论这一活动，因此这个词描述倾向于它的个人。

senses.title: Eager to test claims by argument
senses.titleCN: 热衷于用论证检验主张的
senses.definition: ready to challenge and examine ideas through reasoned exchange
senses.definitionCN: 愿意通过有理由的交流来质疑与检验观点
senses.example: She is argumentative in the best sense: she tests every claim.
senses.exampleCN: 她是最好的那种好辩：每个主张都要检验。
senses.why: The same tendency can be valued rather than blamed when the arguing is disciplined by reasons.
senses.whyCN: 当争论受理由约束时，同一种倾向可以被肯定而不是被责备。

senses.title: Presenting reasons in writing or speech
senses.titleCN: 在写作或言谈中提出理由的
senses.definition: of a text or speech, organized to support a position with reasons
senses.definitionCN: 指文本或演讲，组织起来用理由支持某个立场
senses.example: The assignment is an argumentative essay, not a report.
senses.exampleCN: 这项作业是议论文，不是报告。
senses.why: A genre can be named by its dominant activity, so a text built from arguments is argumentative.
senses.whyCN: 一种体裁可以按其主导活动命名，因此由论证构成的文本就是论证性的。

senses.title: Persuasive in purpose
senses.definition: designed to persuade an audience by appealing to reasons and values
senses.definitionCN: 通过诉诸理由与价值来试图说服受众
senses.example: Her argumentative strategy appealed to shared values.
senses.exampleCN: 她的说服策略诉诸共同价值。
senses.why: Argument aims at assent, so a text that argues is also a text that tries to move the reader.
senses.whyCN: 论证以获致认同为目标，因此进行论证的文本也是试图打动读者的文本。

senses.title: Concerning the structure of arguments
senses.definition: in logic and rhetoric, relating to the form and validity of arguments
senses.definitionCN: 在逻辑与修辞学中，与论证的形式和有效性有关
senses.example: The course covers argumentative validity and fallacy.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课讲授论证的有效性与谬误。
senses.why: A discipline can study the object named by the base, so the adjective labels work about arguments themselves.
senses.whyCN: 一门学科可以研究词基所命名的对象，因此这个形容词标记关于论证本身的工作。

senses.title: Contested in legal style
senses.titleCN: 法律文书中带争辩性的
senses.definition: of a legal document, setting out a contested position rather than merely recording facts
senses.definitionCN: 指法律文书陈述有争议的立场，而不只是记录事实
senses.example: The brief is argumentative rather than neutral.
senses.exampleCN: 这份书状是争辩性的，而不是中立的。
senses.why: Law separates neutral records from documents that press a case, and the adjective marks the latter.
senses.whyCN: 法律把中立记录与推动主张的文书分开，这个形容词标记后者。

senses.title: Combative in tone
senses.definition: carrying a tone of challenge or confrontation in discussion
senses.definitionCN: 在讨论中带有挑战或对抗的语气
senses.example: The meeting grew argumentative after the budget was raised.
senses.exampleCN: 预算被提出后，会议变得火药味十足。
senses.why: Tone is the emotional colour of an exchange, and a quarrelsome colour makes the exchange argumentative.
senses.whyCN: 语气是交流的情绪色彩，好争的色彩使交流变得火药味十足。

senses.title: Open to dispute as a topic
senses.definition: describing a question or issue on which reasonable people can disagree
senses.definitionCN: 描述一个通情达理的人也可能有分歧的问题或议题
senses.example: Whether the policy helped remains an argumentative question.
senses.exampleCN: 这项政策是否有帮助仍是一个可争辩的问题。
senses.why: Some questions invite argument rather than settle it, and the adjective names that openness.
senses.whyCN: 有些问题招来论证而不是被解决，这个形容词命名的正是这种开放性。

intro.en: Argumentative is formed from argument plus the Latin-derived suffix -ative, which marks a tendency. Argument itself comes from Latin argumentum 'proof'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: argumentative 由 argument 加源自拉丁语、标记倾向的后缀构成。argument 本身来自拉丁语 argumentum「证明」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Arguere meant 'to make clear, prove, accuse'; its pre-Latin origin is uncertain, and the root sometimes proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: arguere 意为「使清楚、证明、指控」；其在拉丁语之前的来源不确定，常为它提出的词根是重构。

items.en: Argumentum named proof, evidence and the matter under dispute, and passed through French into English.
items.cn: argumentum 指证明、证据与争议事项，并经法语进入英语。

items.en: The suffix -ativus formed adjectives of tendency or function, saying what something is inclined to do.
items.cn: 拉丁形容词后缀构成表示倾向或功能的形容词，说明某物倾向于做什么。

items.en: English argumentative is recorded in the seventeenth century, first describing a person given to arguing.
items.cn: 英语 argumentative 在十七世纪见于记录，最初描述爱争论的人。

items.en: Later it became a standard label for a kind of essay or speech that presents reasons for a position.
items.cn: 后来它成为标准标签，指一种提出理由支持立场的文章或演讲。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first citation is not fixed, and the pre-Latin origin of arguere remains unsettled; proposed root forms are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定：确切的最早书证没有定论，arguere 在拉丁语之前的来源也未确定；提出的词根形式属重构。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes built with different roots or different suffixes; group two holds near synonyms for a quarrelsome or persuasive manner.
note.cn: 第一组是用不同词根或不同后缀构成的外形相近词；第二组是表示好争或说服态度的近义词。

entries.definition: It looks parallel but comes from a verb meaning 'to increase', so it means adding or enlarging, not arguing.
entries.definitionCN: 看起来结构平行，但来自表示「增加」的动词，因此意思是增添或扩大，不是争论。

entries.definition: It comes from a word for a source of power or expertise and means commanding trust, not fond of argument.
entries.definitionCN: 来自表示权力或专业来源的词，意为有权威的，而不是爱争论的。

entries.definition: It names the process of building arguments; the adjective describes a person or text characterized by that process.
entries.definitionCN: 命名构建论证的过程；这个形容词描述以该过程为特征的人或文本。

entries.definition: The noun names the case or the dispute itself, while the adjective describes the tendency or the genre.
entries.definitionCN: 名词命名论证或争论本身，而形容词描述倾向或体裁。

entries.definition: It stresses readiness for conflict; argumentative can be intellectual and need not be hostile.
entries.definitionCN: 强调准备冲突；argumentative 可以是智识性的，不必敌对。

entries.definition: It describes an issue that causes disagreement or a person who likes it; argumentative focuses on the act of arguing.
entries.definitionCN: 描述引起分歧的议题或喜欢分歧的人；argumentative 聚焦于争论行为。

entries.definition: It means inclined to pick quarrels; argumentative can carry no moral blame at all.
entries.definitionCN: 意为动辄找茬争吵；argumentative 可以完全不含道德责备。

entries.definition: It describes the power to move an audience; an argumentative text aims at this but may fail.
entries.definitionCN: 描述打动受众的力量；论证性文本以此为目标，但可能失败。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the tendency suffix, the two faces of arguing and the academic genre.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示倾向的后缀、争论的两副面孔与学术体裁。

normal.en: The suffix means 'tending to', so the word means tending to argue.
normal.cn: 后缀意为「倾向于」，因此这个词意为倾向于争论。

normal.en: Two faces: quarrelsome at the dinner table, reasoned in the seminar room.
normal.cn: 两副面孔：餐桌上好吵，研讨室里讲理。

normal.en: Academic use: an argumentative essay takes a side and defends it with reasons.
normal.cn: 学术用法：议论文选一边，并用理由为之辩护。

normal.en: Law use: an argumentative brief presses a case rather than recording facts.
normal.cn: 法律用法：争辩性书状推动主张，而不是记录事实。

normal.en: The look-alike with a different root means 'increasing', not 'arguing'.
normal.cn: 外形相近而词根不同的那个词意为「增加的」，而不是「争论的」。

abstract.en: Picture a person carrying a stack of reasons like a shield.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人把一叠理由像盾牌一样举在身前。

abstract.en: Picture a dinner table that turns into a debating chamber.
abstract.cn: 想象一张餐桌变成辩论场。

abstract.en: Picture an essay with a spine made of because-sentences.
abstract.cn: 想象一篇文章的脊梁由一串「因为」句构成。

examples.en: The tutor asked for an argumentative thesis, not a list of facts.
examples.cn: 导师要求一个有论证的论点，而不是一串事实。

examples.en: He became argumentative whenever the topic turned to money.
examples.cn: 每当话题转到钱，他就变得爱争论。

examples.en: The question is genuinely argumentative, with strong cases on both sides.
examples.cn: 这个问题确实可争辩，双方都有有力论证。

dict_mnemonic.text: 论证加「倾向」——一开口就要论个明白 → 爱争论的、论证性的

root: 英语 argument 加源自拉丁语、表示倾向的后缀；argument 来自拉丁语 argumentum「证明」，再上溯 arguere「使清楚、证明、指控」。arguere 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses apply one tendency to a temper, a disciplined habit, a writing genre, a persuasive aim, a logical study, a legal style, a tone and an open question.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一种倾向用于脾气、受约束的习惯、写作文体、说服目的、逻辑研究、法律风格、语气与开放问题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person holding a stack of reasons, ready to push back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人举着一叠理由，随时准备推回去。

branches.en: TEMPER AND TONE: a quarrelsome habit and a combative tone are the hot face of the same tendency.
branches.cn: 脾气与语气：好吵的习惯与好斗的语气，是同一倾向的热面孔。

branches.en: DISCIPLINED HABIT: the same readiness can be turned toward testing claims rather than winning.
branches.cn: 受约束的习惯：同一种准备可以转向检验主张，而不是争胜。

branches.en: GENRE AND OPEN QUESTION: an essay built from reasons and an issue that invites reasons share the structure of argument.
branches.cn: 文体与开放问题：由理由构建的文章与招来理由的议题共享论证结构。

branches.en: PERSUASION: argument aims to move an audience toward assent.
branches.cn: 说服：论证旨在把受众推向认同。

branches.en: FORMAL STUDY AND LAW: logic studies the structure, and law presses a contested position.
branches.cn: 形式研究与法律：逻辑研究结构，法律推动有争议的立场。

intro.en: Argumentative joins the argument noun to a suffix of tendency, and the family ranges from the verb argue to the process noun argumentation.
intro.cn: argumentative 把 argument 这一名词接到表示倾向的后缀上，词族从动词 argue 延伸到过程名词 argumentation。

latinIntro.en: Latin argumentum and the suffix -ativus form the adjective; the deeper root arguere means 'to make clear, prove, accuse'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 argumentum 与形容词后缀构成这个形容词；更深的词根 arguere 意为「使清楚、证明、指控」。

items.example: The argument needs a clearer conclusion.
items.exampleCN: 这个论证需要更清楚的结论。

items.example: The suffix marks a habitual direction.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记习惯性的方向。

items.example: The debate became argumentative.
items.exampleCN: 辩论变得火药味十足。

items.example: He answered argumentatively.
items.exampleCN: 他带着争辩的口气回答。

items.example: Her argumentativeness hid a careful mind.
items.exampleCN: 她的好争辩掩盖了一颗细致的头脑。

items.example: Argumentation is a teachable skill.
items.exampleCN: 论证是一种可教的技能。

items.example: They argued the point for an hour.

items.example: The look-alike suffix hides a different root.

definition_zh: n. 痢疾；细菌性痢疾；阿米巴痢疾
definition_en: an infection of the intestines that causes severe diarrhoea with blood and mucus, spread mainly through contaminated food and water
core_image: 野战医院病历卡上一天十几次带血黏液的腹泻记录；被洪水淹过的井边压水泵贴着「煮沸再饮」的告示；显微镜载玻片上一个圆形细胞里裹着红细胞；村口隔离棚的石灰线

sceneCN: 这里 dysentery 指「引起带血黏液腹泻的肠道感染」（第 1 个义项：痢疾）；句意是营地暴发了痢疾。图中可辨识物件：病历卡、诊断栏、医生的笔尖。

senses.title: An intestinal infection
senses.definition: an infection of the intestines causing severe diarrhoea with blood and mucus
senses.definitionCN: （名词）引起带血与黏液的重度腹泻的肠道感染
senses.example: The camp was hit by an outbreak of dysentery.
senses.exampleCN: 营地暴发了痢疾。

senses.example: Bacillary dysentery spread through the village after the well was flooded.

senses.why: A hand pump beside a flooded latrine with a notice telling people to boil every cup.
senses.whyCN: 被淹的厕所旁有一台压水泵，告示上写着每一杯都要煮沸。

senses.title: The amoebic form
senses.definition: the form caused by an amoeba, often lasting longer and returning
senses.definitionCN: （名词）由阿米巴原虫引起、往往迁延更久且易复发的类型
senses.example: Amoebic dysentery kept returning until the parasite was finally cleared.
senses.exampleCN: 阿米巴痢疾反复发作，直到原虫被彻底清除。
senses.why: A microscope slide shows a round cell with a swallowed red blood cell inside it.

intro.en: Dysentery is Greek dys- meaning bad plus enteron meaning intestine; the same enteron gives enteric and enteritis, so the whole family names the gut and what goes wrong in it.
intro.cn: dysentery 由希腊语 dys-（坏）加 enteron（肠）构成；同一个 enteron 给出 enteric 与 enteritis，所以整个词族都在指称肠以及肠里出的问题。

items.en: The Greek prefix dys- means bad or difficult.
items.cn: 希腊语前缀 dys- 意为坏、困难。

items.en: Greek enteron means intestine, the root of the whole family.
items.cn: 希腊语 enteron 意为肠，是整个词族的词根。

items.en: Greek dysenteria joined the two parts into a name for the illness.
items.cn: 希腊语 dysenteria 把两部分合成病名。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek term unchanged for medical writing.
items.cn: 拉丁语原样借入这个希腊词，用于医学著述。

items.en: Middle English took the word from Latin and Old French.
items.cn: 中古英语从拉丁语与古法语吸收了这个词。

items.en: Medicine separated the bacillary form from the amoebic form.
items.cn: 医学把细菌性与阿米巴性两种痢疾区分开来。

note.en: Dysentery shares the prefix dys- with dysfunction and dyspepsia, and the root enter- with enteric and enteritis; its neighbours name other gut illnesses.
note.cn: dysentery 与 dysfunction、dyspepsia 共用前缀 dys-，与 enteric、enteritis 共用词根 enter-；它的近义词则指称其他肠道疾病。

dict_mnemonic.text: dysentery ＝ dys-（坏、困难）＋ enter-（肠，希腊语 enteron）＋ -ia（疾病）＝「肠子出了坏毛病」。记住 enter- 就记住一串：enteric 肠的、enteritis 肠炎、gastroenteritis 胃肠炎（gastr- 胃）。dys- 家族还有 dysfunction 功能障碍、dyspepsia 消化不良、dyslexia 读写困难。临床上分两型：bacillary dysentery 细菌性（志贺菌，经污染食物与水传播），amoebic dysentery 阿米巴性（原虫，病程更长易复发）。关键特征是带血与黏液的腹泻，普通 diarrhoea 只是稀便，未必带血。

root: 希腊语 dys-（坏）＋ enteron（肠）→ dysenteria → 拉丁语 dysenteria → dysentery（痢疾）
