definition_zh: 制造业；制造过程；制造业的
definition_en: the business and process of making goods in quantity from raw materials, usually in factories
core_image: 钢卷沿辊道送进压机，压成车身侧板，火花顺着传送带一路落下
scene: 厂房里钢卷被压成车身侧板，火花沿着传送带一路闪烁。 Manufacturing employs more people in this valley than farming does.
sceneCN: 句中的说法指「以工厂批量生产商品的整个行业与活动」（第 1 个义项：把原料加工成成品的经济部门）；句意为在这个河谷里，制造业雇用的人比农业多。图中可辨识物件：钢卷、压机、车身侧板、火花与传送带。

pos.zh: 制造业；制造过程（不可数）
制造业的；制造方面的

senses.title: The sector as a whole
senses.definition: the branch of the economy that makes goods in factories
senses.definitionCN: 在工厂里制造商品的那一经济部门
senses.example: Manufacturing employs more people in this valley than farming does.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个河谷里，制造业雇用的人比农业多。
senses.why: The activity is named with a noun of process, and a whole sector takes the name of its characteristic activity.
senses.whyCN: 这项活动用表示过程的名词命名，整个部门便以它最具代表性的活动为名。

senses.title: The act of making goods
senses.definition: the process by which raw materials become finished goods
senses.definitionCN: 原料变成成品的过程
senses.example: Manufacturing of the wing takes eleven hours per unit.
senses.exampleCN: 每件机翼的制造需要十一小时。
senses.why: The noun of process names the doing itself, which is why it can be timed per unit.
senses.whyCN: 这个表示过程的名词指「做」本身，因此可以按件计时。

senses.title: The stage after design
senses.titleCN: 制造环节（相对于设计与销售）
senses.definition: the stage of production, as distinct from design, marketing or service
senses.definitionCN: 生产阶段，与设计、营销或服务相区别
senses.example: Design is done here, but manufacturing happens overseas.
senses.exampleCN: 设计在这里做，制造则在海外。
senses.why: A long chain of work is divided into stages, and the stage that turns drawings into objects takes this name.
senses.whyCN: 漫长的工作链被分成阶段，把图纸变成实物的那一阶段取了这个名称。

senses.title: Factory production as opposed to craft
senses.titleCN: 工业制造（与手工业相对）
senses.definition: machine-based production in quantity, as opposed to making by hand
senses.definitionCN: 以机器批量生产，与手工制作相对
senses.example: Cheap manufacturing replaced the village workshops.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价的工业制造取代了村里的作坊。
senses.why: The word entered English for goods made by hand, then shifted to the factory system that replaced handwork.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指手工制品，后来转向取代手工的工厂体系。

senses.title: The methods used to make things
senses.definition: the organised methods, such as lean production, by which goods are made
senses.definitionCN: 制造商品所用的有组织方法，如精益生产
senses.example: Lean manufacturing cut waste at every station.
senses.exampleCN: 精益制造削减了每个工位的浪费。
senses.why: Once the activity is studied, its methods are also called by the name, with adjectives to mark the variant.
senses.whyCN: 这项活动被研究之后，其方法也用同一名称称呼，再加形容词标出变体。

senses.title: The measured output of factories
senses.definition: the volume of goods produced, reported as an economic figure
senses.definitionCN: 所生产商品的数量，作为经济数字发布
senses.example: Manufacturing rose for a fourth quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 制造业产出连续第四个季度上升。
senses.why: Statistical offices count the activity and report its size, so the same noun becomes a number in the news.
senses.whyCN: 统计部门计量这项活动并报告其规模，因此同一名词在新闻里变成一个数字。

senses.title: Factory jobs taken together
senses.definition: employment in factories, treated as one block in labour statistics
senses.definitionCN: 工厂中的就业，在劳动力统计中被当作一整块
senses.example: Manufacturing shed two thousand jobs in the county.
senses.exampleCN: 该县制造业减少了二千个岗位。
senses.why: Jobs follow the sector, so the sector's name also stands for the people it employs.
senses.whyCN: 岗位跟着部门走，因此部门名称也代表它所雇用的人。

senses.title: Used as a modifier
senses.definition: placed before another noun to mark the part of the economy concerned
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词前，标出所涉的经济部分
senses.example: The manufacturing sector asked for cheaper power.
senses.exampleCN: 制造业部门要求更便宜的电价。
senses.why: A noun used before another noun turns into a description, which is how the word works as an adjective.
senses.whyCN: 名词放在另一名词前就成了描述语，这个词作形容词时正是如此。

intro.en: Manufacturing is the noun of process from a French-derived verb whose Latin base means 'made by hand'. Its sense moved from handwork to factory work. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这是一个法语来源动词的过程名词，其拉丁底子意为「用手做成」。词义从手工制品转向工厂生产。年代均为约数。

items.en: Manus meant 'hand'. Its deeper root is reconstructed, so source uncertain below Latin.
items.cn: manus 意为「手」。其更深词根属重构形式，故拉丁语以下来源不确定。

items.en: Facere meant 'to make, to do'. Its pre-Latin root is also a reconstruction.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、制作」。其在拉丁语之前的词根同样属重构形式。

items.en: The phrase manu factum meant 'made by hand', and it named work done with skill rather than by nature.
items.cn: 短语 manu factum 意为「用手做成」，指凭技艺而非天然生成之物。

items.en: French manufacture turned the phrase into a noun in the seventeenth century, and English borrowed it for things made by hand.
items.cn: 法语 manufacture 在十七世纪把这个短语变成名词，英语借它指手工制品。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the same noun moved to machine production in factories, and the process noun took the sector with it.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，同一名词转向工厂里的机器生产，过程名词也随之带上了整个部门的意思。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same verb in different grammatical roles; group two holds nouns for making goods.
note.cn: 第一组是同一动词在不同语法角色下的形式；第二组是表示「制造商品」的名词。

entries.definition: The verb for making goods, and as a noun either the act or the products; it does not name the industry.
entries.definitionCN: 指制造商品的动词，作名词时指动作或产品，但不指整个行业。

entries.definition: The company that carries out the work, formed with the agent suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 用施动后缀构成，指从事这项工作的公司。

entries.definition: Made in a factory, or invented rather than true; the participle carries both senses.
entries.definitionCN: 指工厂制成的，也指捏造而非真实的，两种意思都在这个分词里。

entries.tag: an old word for a factory
entries.definition: A nineteenth-century word for a factory building, now rare and historical.
entries.definitionCN: 十九世纪指工厂建筑的词，现已罕用，属历史词。

entries.definition: The making of goods or services of any kind, including farming and mining.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指商品或服务的生产，包括农业与采矿。

entries.definition: The branch of the economy, which may include extraction as well as making.
entries.definitionCN: 指经济部门，可能既包括采掘也包括制造。

entries.definition: The assembly of a structure from prepared parts, often on site.
entries.definitionCN: 用预制部件组装结构，常在现场进行。

entries.definition: The stage where components are joined, one part of manufacturing rather than the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 把零件接合起来的阶段，是制造的一部分，而非全部。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Latin phrase for 'made by hand' became a French noun, and English added a process ending to it.
normal.cn: 拉丁语「用手做成」的说法变成法语名词，英语再给它加过程后缀。

normal.en: The family runs manufacture, manufacturer, manufactured and the adjective for what can be made.
normal.cn: 同族词包括制造、制造商、制成的，以及表示「可制造的」形容词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: sector, industry, process, plant, costs, lean production.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出领域：制造业部门、制造业、制造过程、制造厂、制造成本、精益制造。

normal.en: The word began as praise for handwork and ended as the name of the system that replaced it.
normal.cn: 这个词起初是对手工的赞许，最后成了取代手工的那套体系的名字。

normal.en: Governments report it as a number, and unions speak of it as jobs, but both mean the same factories.
normal.cn: 政府把它报成一个数字，工会把它说成岗位，但两者都指同一批工厂。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet of steel that becomes a curve without anyone touching it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张钢板在无人触碰的情况下变成一个曲面。

abstract.en: Picture a village of workshops replaced overnight by one long shed.
abstract.cn: 想象一夜之间，一村作坊被一座长厂房取代。

abstract.en: Picture a number in a newspaper standing for thousands of dinner tables.
abstract.cn: 想象报纸上的一个数字，背后是成千上万张饭桌。

examples.en: Manufacturing moved inland as coastal rents rose.
examples.cn: 沿海租金上涨，制造业迁往内陆。

examples.en: The country wants to move from manufacturing to design.
examples.cn: 这个国家想从制造转向设计。

examples.en: Manufacturing output fell while services grew.
examples.cn: 制造业产出下降，而服务业增长。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「manu（手）+ fact（做）+ ing（过程）」——用手做出来的过程 → 制造、制造业

root: 拉丁语中表示「手」的名词与表示「做」的动词构成「用手做成」的短语，经法语变成名词，再加过程后缀；两个词根更早的来源均属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one workshop: an industry is named after its activity, the activity is timed per unit, the stage is placed after design, machine work replaces handwork, the methods are studied and named, output becomes a statistic, jobs become a block, and the word finally works as a modifier.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一间厂房展开：行业以活动得名、活动按件计时、环节排在设计的后头、机器取代手工、方法被研究并命名、产出变成统计数字、岗位成为一整块，最后这个词还用作定语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coil of steel passing under a press and leaving as a curved panel, with sparks falling along the line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一卷钢从压机下经过，出来时已成弯曲的板件，火花沿产线落下。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND SECTOR: the industry and the jobs inside it are one block of work counted two ways.
branches.cn: 人与部门：行业与其中的岗位，是同一块工作被两种方式计数。

branches.en: THE STAGE OF MAKING: the timed process and the stage after design are the same link in a longer chain.
branches.cn: 制造环节：可计时的过程与设计之后的阶段，是长链上的同一环。

branches.en: FROM HAND TO METHOD: machine production replaces the workshop, and then its methods are studied and named.
branches.cn: 从手到方法：机器生产取代作坊，随后其方法被研究并命名。

branches.en: OUTPUT AS A FIGURE: production becomes a number in the news.
branches.cn: 产出作为数字：生产变成新闻里的一个数字。

branches.en: THE MODIFIER: the same noun placed before another word marks which part of the economy is meant.
branches.cn: 定语用法：同一名词放在另一词前，标出所指的是经济中的哪一部分。

intro.en: Manufacturing is a Latin phrase compressed into a French noun and then given an English process ending, so its parts are a word for hand, a verb for making and a suffix for the ongoing act.
intro.cn: 这是一个被压缩成法语名词的拉丁短语，再加英语过程后缀，因此其成分是一个表示「手」的词、一个表示「做」的动词，以及表示持续动作的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin manus gives manual and manage; facere gives factory and fabrication; the two meet in the phrase for made by hand.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示「手」的词衍生出手动的与经营等词；表示「做」的动词衍生出工厂与制作等词；两者在「用手做成」的短语中相遇。

items.example: The root noun supplies the hand that holds the tool.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根名词提供握工具的那只手。

items.structure: facere, feci, factum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The verb supplies the making.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「制作」。

items.example: The phrase is the seed of the whole noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语是整个名词的种子。

items.example: French compressed the phrase into one noun.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个短语压缩成一个名词。

items.structure: -ing (English noun suffix for an action or process)
items.example: The suffix names the activity rather than the object.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀指活动，而非物件。

items.example: The agent suffix names the doer.
items.exampleCN: 施动后缀指施动者。

items.example: The participle also came to mean invented, since both are made.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词也引申为捏造的，因为两者都是「做出来的」。

items.example: The suffix marks feasibility.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记可行性。

definition_zh: 罪犯；违法者；违规者；冒犯他人的人；惹人反感的人；（事故或问题的）罪魁祸首
definition_en: a person who commits a crime or breaks a rule, or who gives offence to others; also the thing chiefly responsible for a problem
core_image: 一个人抬脚跨过地上那道白线，鞋底已经落在禁止的一侧，身上还别着写有名字的牌子
scene: 小区业主会上，大家讨论那位总把垃圾倒进邻家院子的住户，一致认为他是破坏规矩的人。 At the residents' meeting the neighbours agreed that the man who kept dumping rubbish over the fence was an offender.
sceneCN: 这里指「违反规矩、触犯他人的人」，对应第 1 个义项：实施了违法或违规行为的人；句意为业主会上邻居们认定那个反复往邻家院子倒垃圾的人就是破坏规矩者。画面要点：越过白线的脚、写有名字的牌子、倒在界外的垃圾。

pos.zh: 罪犯；违法者；违规者（可数，法律与日常通用）
冒犯者；惹人反感的人（由动词「触怒」加施事后缀而来）
罪魁祸首；主要祸源（可指事物，常用于环境、事故话题）

derivatives.zh: 去掉施事后缀后的动词原形，承拉丁 offendere「撞上、触犯」→ 由「撞到某物」转为「得罪人、违犯法度」
加名词后缀（源自拉丁语，表行为或状态）→ 由「触犯」这一动作转为「所犯之事、违法行为」
美式拼写，同样来自名词后缀（拉丁语中表状态的词尾） → 由动作转为「罪错、犯规」，并引申出「进攻」义
加形容词后缀（源自拉丁语，表倾向或性质）→ 由「触犯」转为「带有冒犯性的、令人不快的」
加否定前缀于 offensive → 由「会冒犯人」转为「不惹人反感的、无害的」

senses.title: A person who commits a crime
senses.definition: a person who has committed a crime, especially one identified in legal or police records
senses.definitionCN: 实施了犯罪行为的人，尤指被法律或警方记录在案者
senses.example: At the residents' meeting the neighbours agreed that the man who kept dumping rubbish over the fence was an offender.
senses.exampleCN: 业主会上，邻居们认定那个反复往邻家院子倒垃圾的人就是违法者。
senses.why: The Latin verb offendere meant 'to strike against' something, and -er names the one who does it; a criminal is literally the person who has struck against the line the law drew.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 offendere 意为「撞上某物」，这个后缀指做出该动作的人；罪犯字面上就是撞到法律所画那道线的人。

senses.title: A person who breaks a rule, not a law
senses.titleCN: 违反规章而非法律的人
senses.definition: a person who contravenes the rules of an institution, sport or workplace without necessarily committing a crime
senses.definitionCN: 违反机构、运动或工作场所规章的人，未必构成犯罪
senses.example: A student who copies another's essay is an offender under the school's honesty code.
senses.exampleCN: 抄袭他人文章的学生，按学校诚信守则属于违规者。
senses.why: The line crossed need not be a statute; any drawn boundary, from a school code to a game's rules, produces an offender when someone steps over it.
senses.whyCN: 被越过的那条线不必是成文法；从校规到比赛规则，只要有人踩过任何画出的界线，就产生一个违规者。

senses.title: A person who gives offence by words
senses.definition: a person whose remarks or behaviour wound or insult someone
senses.definitionCN: 因言语或举止刺伤、侮辱他人而冒犯对方的人
senses.example: His jokes made him an offender in the eyes of the older guests.
senses.exampleCN: 他的玩笑使他在年长宾客眼中成了冒犯者。
senses.why: To offend was also to strike someone's feelings; the same -er suffix turns that blow into a person, so offence is no longer a line on the ground but a wound in another mind.
senses.whyCN: offend 也有「击伤他人感受」之义；同一个施事后缀把这一击落回到人身上，冒犯便从地上的线变成他人心里的伤。

senses.title: A person who disgusts or annoys
senses.definition: a person who is widely regarded as unpleasant or troublesome
senses.definitionCN: 被众人视为讨厌、惹麻烦的人
senses.example: In the office he was the offender whom nobody wanted to sit beside.
senses.exampleCN: 在办公室里，他是那个谁都不愿挨着坐的讨厌鬼。
senses.why: The physical core survives as social discomfort: the one who keeps bumping into other people's comfort is felt as an offender even when no rule is written.
senses.whyCN: 物理上的核心意象转为社交不适：总撞到别人舒适区的人，即使没有明文规定，也会被感觉成冒犯者。

senses.title: The chief source of a problem
senses.definition: the thing most responsible for a fault, a pollution or an accident
senses.definitionCN: 对某一缺陷、污染或事故负主要责任的事物
senses.example: Plastic packaging is the biggest offender in household waste.
senses.exampleCN: 塑料包装是生活垃圾中最大的祸源。
senses.why: Once the label applies to causes rather than persons, the guilty party can be a material; what 'strikes against' cleanliness takes the role of the offender.
senses.whyCN: 当这一标签从人转向原因，肇事者可以是某种材料；撞向洁净之物的东西便顶上了祸源的角色。

senses.title: A player who commits a foul
senses.definition: an athlete who commits an illegal move and is penalised by the referee
senses.definitionCN: 做出违规动作并被裁判处罚的运动员
senses.example: The referee sent the offender to the bench for two minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判把犯规者罚到替补席上坐两分钟。
senses.why: A playing field is the clearest case of a line drawn on the ground, so the sports sense keeps the original picture almost unchanged.
senses.whyCN: 球场是最典型的「在地上画线」的场合，因此体育义几乎原封不动地保留了最初的画面。

senses.title: The person named in a charge
senses.titleCN: 指控文书中被点名的一方
senses.definition: the person identified in a legal charge before any finding of guilt
senses.definitionCN: 在尚未判定有罪之前，被法律指控文书点名的人
senses.example: The report names the alleged offender but protects the victim.
senses.exampleCN: 报道点出了被指控者，却保护了受害者的身份。
senses.why: Legal drafting needs a neutral noun for the party on the wrong side of the line; offender supplies it without yet asserting guilt.
senses.whyCN: 法律文书需要一个中性名词来称呼站在界线错侧的一方，offender 正好提供这一称呼，同时并不预先断定有罪。

senses.title: One who breaks a moral or sacred law
senses.titleCN: 违背道德或神圣律法的人
senses.definition: a person who transgresses a moral, religious or conscience-bound standard
senses.definitionCN: 违背道德、宗教或良心准则的人
senses.example: In the old sermon he was called an offender against heaven itself.
senses.exampleCN: 在那篇古老的布道中，他被称为连上天都敢触犯的人。
senses.why: The line can be drawn by God rather than by a state; the oldest use of offendere in religious writing already meant to stumble against a sacred order.
senses.whyCN: 这条线也可以由神明而非国家来画；offendere 在宗教文献里最早的用法本就指撞向神圣秩序而失足。

intro.en: Offender is English offend plus the agent suffix -er. Offend came through Old French from Latin offendere 'to strike against, stumble', a compound of ob- 'against' and a verb of striking. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: offender 是英语动词 offend 加施事后缀构成。offend 经古法语来自拉丁 offendere「撞上、失足」，由表「对着」的前缀与一个表「撞击」的动词复合而成。年代均为约数。

items.en: The prefix ob- meant 'toward, against, in the way of', and it marks the direction of a collision rather than its cause.
items.cn: 这个前缀意为「朝向、对着、挡在路上」，它标出撞击的方向，而非撞击的成因。

items.en: Offendere meant 'to strike against, hit, stumble', and by extension 'to commit a fault'; it was built from ob- plus a verb of striking.
items.cn: offendere 意为「撞上、击中、失足」，引申为「犯过错」；由一个表「对着」的前缀加一个表撞击的动词构成。

items.en: The participle offensa 'a striking against' supplied the noun for a fault, the ancestor of English offence and offense.
items.cn: 分词形式 offensa 意为「撞上」，提供表示过错的名词，是英语 offence 与 offense 的前身。

items.en: Old French took the verb as offendre and passed it to English in the fourteenth century with the sense 'to commit a sin or fault'.
items.cn: 古法语把该动词作 offendre 吸收，并于十四世纪传给英语，当时意为「犯下罪过或过失」。

items.en: Adding -er to the verb produced offender, first for a sinner before a court of law, then for any person who breaks a rule.
items.cn: 在动词后加施事后缀构成 offender，最初指在法庭上被审的罪人，后泛指任何破坏规则的人。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century statutes fixed phrases such as repeat offender and young offender, while environmental writing extended the word to things.
items.cn: 十九、二十世纪的法条固定了「惯犯」「未成年犯」等说法，环境类写作又把该词扩展到事物身上。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb of striking and shows how far its family spread; the second group offers near alternatives for a person who does wrong.
note.cn: 第一组共享那个表「撞击」的拉丁动词，可见其词族分布之广；第二组是「做错事的人」的近义替代。

entries.definition: To break a law or to hurt someone's feelings; it is the verb from which the person-noun is built.
entries.definitionCN: 违反法律或伤害他人感情；它是派生人称名词所依托的动词。

entries.definition: The act of breaking a law or the feeling of being insulted; it names the deed, not the doer.
entries.definitionCN: 违法或冒犯的行为，也指被冒犯的感受；它指行为，不指行为人。

entries.definition: Causing resentment, or a military attack; the root idea of striking survives in both uses.
entries.definitionCN: 令人反感的，或指军事进攻；「撞击」的词根义在两种用法中都还在。

entries.definition: The party accused in a court case; it is built on defendere 'to ward off', the mirror image of striking against.
entries.definitionCN: 法庭上被指控的一方；由 defendere「挡开」构成，正是「撞上去」的镜像动作。

entries.definition: A person convicted of a crime; it states a legal category, while offender can merely name someone who broke a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 被判定有罪的人；它给出法律类别，而 offender 也可以只指破坏规则者。

entries.definition: The person responsible for a fault or mishap; it stresses blame rather than legal breach.
entries.definitionCN: 对过失或事故负有责任的人；它强调该受责怪，而非法律上的违犯。

entries.definition: A person who does something morally wrong; the judgement is ethical, not statutory.
entries.definitionCN: 做了道德上错事的人；其判断是伦理性的，而非法条性的。

entries.definition: A person who steps beyond a set limit or command; it keeps the image of crossing a line but sounds formal.
entries.definitionCN: 越过既定界限或命令的人；它保留「越过界线」的意象，但语体正式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin verb, the real agent suffix and the real fixed phrases of law and sport.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词、真实的施事后缀，以及法律与体育中的真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Offendere is 'to strike against'; add -er and you have the one who strikes against the line.
normal.cn: offendere 意为「撞上去」；加上施事后缀就是那个撞向界线的人。

normal.en: The ob- in offend means 'against', the same direction seen in oppose and object.
normal.cn: offend 中那个表「对着」的前缀意为「对着」，与 oppose、object 中的方向感相同。

normal.en: Fixed phrases sort people by repetition: first-time offender, repeat offender, habitual offender.
normal.cn: 固定搭配按次数给人分类：初犯、屡犯、习惯性违法者。

normal.en: Offence is the deed, offender is the doer, offensive is the quality: one root, three jobs.
normal.cn: offence 是事，offender 是人，offensive 是性质：一个词根，三种职务。

normal.en: In sport the offender is simply the player who crossed the line the referee watches.
normal.cn: 在体育中，犯规者就是那个越过裁判所盯那条线的球员。

abstract.en: Picture a chalk line on a pavement and a shoe sole landing just past it, the dust still rising.
abstract.cn: 想象人行道上一条粉笔线，一只鞋底刚落到线外，尘土还未落下。

abstract.en: Picture a name tag pinned on a coat before the wearer has even entered the room.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚名牌在本人还没进屋之前就已别在了外套上。

abstract.en: Picture a broken fence with a single footprint on the forbidden side of the grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一段破损的栅栏，草地禁入的一侧只有一个脚印。

examples.en: The police recorded the offender's fingerprints and released him pending trial.
examples.cn: 警方录下该罪犯的指纹，随后在候审期间将其释放。

examples.en: Any offender caught smuggling will lose the licence for good.
examples.cn: 任何被查获走私的违法者都将永久失去执照。

examples.en: The report calls the city's ageing sewers the main offender in the flooding.
examples.cn: 报告称城中老化的下水道是此次内涝的主要祸源。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，犯的」——哦，这事原来是他犯下的：跨过界线、犯下过错的那个人 → 罪犯、违规者

root: 拉丁语表「对着」的前缀 + 表撞击的词干 → offendere「撞上、失足、犯过」→ 古法语 offendre → 英语 offend；加表施事者的后缀 → offender，即「撞到界线上的那个人」；同族有 offence、offense、offensive、defendant。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses start from one picture: a person stepping over a drawn line. The line may be a statute, a school code, someone's feelings, a game's rules, a charge sheet or a sacred order; whenever it is crossed, the one who crossed it is the offender.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都始于同一幅画面：一个人跨过画好的线。这条线可以是成文法、校规、他人的感受、比赛规则、指控文书或神圣秩序；只要有线被越过，越线者就是 offender。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person whose shoe has just landed on the forbidden side of a chalk line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人的鞋底刚落在粉笔线外的那一侧。

branches.en: STATUTE: the line is a law, and the one who crosses it is a criminal in the eyes of the court.
branches.cn: 成文法：线是法律，越线者在法庭眼中即罪犯。

branches.en: RULES OF PLAY: school codes and referees' whistles draw thinner lines, yet crossing them still makes an offender.
branches.cn: 游戏规则：校规与裁判的哨声画出更细的线，越过它们同样成为违规者。

branches.en: SOCIAL WOUND: the line becomes another person's comfort, and the one who keeps bumping it is felt as offensive.
branches.cn: 社交伤害：线变成他人的舒适边界，反复撞上去的人便被视为冒犯者。

branches.en: BLAME SHIFTED: when the guilty party is a material or a practice, the word lends its blame to things.
branches.cn: 归责转移：当肇事者是材料或做法时，这个词把自己的责难借给了事物。

branches.en: FORMAL AND SACRED LABELS: legal drafting and religious language keep the noun for the party on the wrong side, before or beyond any trial.
branches.cn: 正式与神圣标签：法律文书与宗教语言把这个名词留给站在错侧的一方，无论审前还是超越审判。

intro.en: Offender is a transparent English build: a Latin verb of striking plus the agent suffix -er, with older relatives showing the same prefix at work.
intro.cn: offender 的构造清楚可拆：一个表「撞击」的拉丁动词，加上施事后缀；更早的同族词展示了同一前缀的作用。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family around offendere includes offensa, offensio and the verb itself; the prefix ob- also appears in object and oppose.
latinIntro.cn: offendere 周围的拉丁词族包括 offensa、offensio 与动词本身；这个前缀也见于 object 与 oppose。

items.example: The prefix turns a neutral motion into a collision.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把中性的移动变成了撞击。

items.meaning: to strike against; to commit a fault
items.example: Loud remarks may offend a listener.
items.exampleCN: 大声的评论可能冒犯听者。

items.meaning: a person or thing that performs the action
items.example: The suffix is added straight to the verb stem.
items.exampleCN: 该后缀直接加在动词词干之后。

items.meaning: a person who breaks a law or rule
items.example: The offender was charged the next morning.
items.exampleCN: 该违法者第二天早上被起诉。

items.meaning: several people who break the same line
items.example: Young offenders receive separate treatment.
items.exampleCN: 未成年犯会受到另行处理。

items.meaning: the act of breaking a law; a feeling of hurt
items.meaningCN: 违法行为；被冒犯的感受
items.example: Driving without a licence is an offence.
items.exampleCN: 无照驾驶是一项违法行为。

items.meaningCN: 引人反感的；用于进攻的
items.example: The poster used offensive language.
items.exampleCN: 那张海报用了冒犯性语言。

items.example: He kept the talk inoffensive.
items.exampleCN: 他让谈话保持在无害的范围。

items.example: The defendant denied the charge.
items.exampleCN: 被告否认了指控。

items.example: The team took a defensive stance.
items.exampleCN: 该队采取了防守姿态。

latinEntries.meaning: to strike against; to stumble; to commit a fault

definition_zh: 教条；教义；不容置疑的信条
definition_en: a belief or set of beliefs accepted as certainly true, often without evidence or question
core_image: 教堂里一块刻满字的大石板，人人从它前面走过，没有人停下来读第二遍
scene: 教室里老师说这条规则不可讨论，全班安静下来。 Nobody dared to question the dogma of the department.
sceneCN: 这里 dogma 指不容置疑的信条（第 1 个义项：被当作确定真理的信念）；句意为没人敢质疑系里那条铁律。

pos.zh: 教条；教义；信条

senses.title: Fixed doctrine
senses.definition: a principle held as certainly true and placed beyond discussion
senses.definitionCN: 被当作确定真理、置于讨论之外的原则
senses.example: Nobody dared to question the dogma of the department.
senses.exampleCN: 没人敢质疑系里那条铁律。
senses.why: The word marks not the content of a belief but its status: closed to argument.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标记的不是信念的内容，而是它的地位：对论证关闭。

senses.title: Church teaching
senses.definition: an official teaching of a church that members must accept
senses.definitionCN: 教会官方教导、成员必须接受的教义
senses.example: The council restated the dogma on the Trinity.
senses.exampleCN: 会议重申了关于三位一体的教义。
senses.why: In religious use the word is neutral: a teaching received, not an insult.
senses.whyCN: 在宗教用法中，这个词是中性的：被领受的教导，而非贬语。

senses.title: Unquestioned belief
senses.definition: an idea accepted by a group without ever being tested
senses.definitionCN: 被一群人不加检验就接受的观念
senses.example: It was dogma that a good degree guaranteed a good job.
senses.exampleCN: 当时有一种信条：好学位必然带来好工作。
senses.why: An untested idea repeated by enough people stops looking like an idea at all.
senses.whyCN: 一个未经检验的观念被足够多的人重复后，就不再像观念了。

senses.title: The party line
senses.definition: the official position that members of a political group must repeat
senses.definitionCN: 政治团体成员必须复述的官方立场
senses.example: He repeated the party dogma word for word.
senses.exampleCN: 他把党的教条一字不差地重复了一遍。
senses.why: Politics shows how a belief becomes a test of loyalty rather than a claim about the world.
senses.whyCN: 政治展示了信念如何变成忠诚的考验，而不是关于世界的断言。

senses.title: Rigid principle
senses.definition: a rule applied mechanically, without regard to the case in front of it
senses.definitionCN: 机械套用、不顾眼前个案的规则
senses.example: The committee applied the dogma and ignored the evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会套用了那条僵化原则，无视证据。
senses.why: When a principle stops listening, it hardens into dogma.
senses.whyCN: 当原则不再倾听，它就硬化为教条。

senses.title: Dogma as comfort
senses.definition: a belief kept because it makes an uncertain world easier to bear
senses.definitionCN: 因能让不确定的世界更易承受而被保留的信念
senses.example: For many, the old dogma was a kind of shelter.
senses.exampleCN: 对许多人来说，旧教条是一种庇护。
senses.why: A settled answer soothes more than an open question, even when the answer is wrong.
senses.whyCN: 一个已定的答案比一个开放的问题更让人安心，即使答案是错的。

senses.title: Rejection of dogma
senses.definition: the stance of refusing beliefs that demand acceptance without reason
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝接受那些要求无条件相信的信念的立场
senses.example: The young scholars were united only in their rejection of dogma.
senses.exampleCN: 这些年轻学者唯一一致的地方就是拒斥教条。
senses.why: Refusing closed beliefs can itself become a shared position, and a shared position can harden.
senses.whyCN: 拒斥封闭的信念本身也可能成为共同立场，而共同立场也会硬化。

senses.title: Dogmatic assertion
senses.definition: a statement delivered as certain in a tone that forbids reply
senses.definitionCN: 以确定无疑、禁止回应的口吻作出的陈述
senses.example: His essay opened with a dogma rather than a question.
senses.exampleCN: 他的文章以一个独断的断言开头，而不是一个问题。
senses.why: Here the word has moved from the belief to the way it is spoken.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词已从信念移到了说出它的方式。

intro.en: Dogma is a Greek word for opinion, and its journey from 'what seems right' to 'what may not be questioned' is the whole story.
intro.cn: dogma 是希腊语中表示「意见」的词，它从「看起来对的」走到「不许质疑的」，整个过程就是这个词的故事。

items.en: Greek dogma meant 'an opinion, a decree', something a person or a city decided to hold.
items.cn: 希腊语 dogma 意为「意见、法令」，是某人或城邦决定持守的东西。

items.en: Dokein 'to seem' is the root: a dogma is what seems true to someone.
items.cn: dokein「显得、看来」是词根：dogma 就是某人觉得为真的东西。

items.en: The early church used it for official teachings, giving the word its neutral religious sense.
items.cn: 早期教会用它指官方教导，赋予这个词中性的宗教含义。

items.en: English took the word in the 16c., and by the 17c. it could already carry a sneer.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个词，到十七世纪它已能带讥讽。

items.en: Today the word usually criticises: a belief held as beyond question is rarely thought healthy.
items.cn: 今天这个词通常带批评：被视为不容置疑的信念很少被认为是健康的。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dogm stem; the near-meaning group moves from neutral teaching to closed conviction.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dogm 词干；近义组从中文性的教导移向封闭的确信。

entries.definition: asserting beliefs as certainly true.
entries.definitionCN: 把信念断言为确定真理的。

entries.definition: the habit of asserting beliefs without evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 无证据断言信念的习惯。

entries.definition: a person who holds beliefs beyond question.
entries.definitionCN: 持不容置疑信念的人。

entries.definition: the Greek plural of dogma.
entries.definitionCN: dogma 的希腊语复数。

entries.definition: a set of beliefs taught by a church or party.
entries.definitionCN: 教会或党派所教导的一套信念。

entries.definition: a formal summary of what a group believes.
entries.definitionCN: 一个团体信念的正式摘要。

entries.definition: the belief officially accepted as correct.
entries.definitionCN: 被官方认定正确的信念。

entries.definition: a principle held as true by a group.
entries.definitionCN: 团体认为为真的一条原则。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a stone slab that people pass without ever stopping to read.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「人们走过一块石板、却从不停下细读」的画面。

normal.en: Dogma and doctor share a d-o-g start but nothing else: a doctor questions, dogma does not.
normal.cn: dogma 与 doctor 都以 d-o 开头，但别无关系：医生会质疑，教条不会。

normal.en: Think of a museum guard who forbids anyone to touch the display.
normal.cn: 想象一位博物馆守卫，禁止任何人触碰展品。

normal.en: Dogma ends in a: a is the first letter, and dogma claims to be the first word.
normal.cn: dogma 以 a 结尾：a 是第一个字母，而教条自称是第一句话。

normal.en: Say DOG-muh; the flat first syllable sounds like a rule read aloud.
normal.cn: 读成 DOG-muh，平直的第一个音节像在朗读一条规则。

normal.en: Link it with doctrine: doctrine is what is taught, dogma is what may not be asked.
normal.cn: 和 doctrine 联系：doctrine 是被教导的，dogma 是不许被追问的。

abstract.en: A belief becomes dogma at the moment questioning it becomes rude.
abstract.cn: 当质疑它变得失礼时，信念就变成了教条。

abstract.en: Dogma saves thought in the short run and costs it in the long run.
abstract.cn: 教条短期省下思考，长期却要付出思考的代价。

abstract.en: Every age has a dogma it cannot see, which is why history is useful.
abstract.cn: 每个时代都有自己看不见的教条，这正是历史有用的原因。

examples.cn: 没人敢质疑系里那条铁律。

examples.cn: 会议重申了关于三位一体的教义。

dict_mnemonic.text: dog（doc，教导）+ ma（名词）：被教导到不许再问的东西，就是「教条」。

root: 希腊语 dogma（意见、法令），源自 dokein（显得、看来）

sensesIntro.en: Dogma always names a belief plus a rule about that belief: it may not be questioned; the senses differ in who enforces the rule.
sensesIntro.cn: dogma 总是命名一个信念，再加上关于这个信念的一条规则：不许质疑；各义项的差别在于是谁在执行这条规则。

core.en: A BELIEF PLACED BEYOND QUESTION
core.cn: 被放到质疑之外的信念

branches.en: The belief and its official religious form.
branches.cn: 信念本身及其正式的宗教形式。

branches.en: Why people keep it: it feels settled and it comforts.
branches.cn: 人们保留它的原因：它显得已定，而且令人安心。

branches.en: How institutions enforce it, in politics and in procedure.
branches.cn: 机构如何执行它，无论在政治还是程序上。

branches.en: The reaction against it, and the tone that gives it away.
branches.cn: 对它的反弹，以及暴露它的那种语气。

branches.en: A principle hardens into dogma when it stops listening.
branches.cn: 原则在不再倾听时硬化为教条。

intro.en: The dogm family describes the closed mind: a belief, the habit of asserting it, and the person who never asks.
intro.cn: dogm 词族描述封闭的心：一个信念，断言它的习惯，以及从不发问的人。

latinIntro.en: Greek dokein, to seem, gives dogma and also docent and document, all tied to what is shown or taught.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 dokein（显得）给出 dogma，也给出 docent 与 document，都与被显示或被教导的东西有关。

items.meaning: a thing held as settled opinion
items.meaningCN: 被当作既定意见持守的东西
items.example: The dogma survived three reforms.
items.exampleCN: 这条教条经历三次改革仍存。

items.example: His dogmatic tone ended the debate.
items.exampleCN: 他独断的语气终结了讨论。

items.example: Dogmatism blocked every question.
items.exampleCN: 教条主义挡住了每一个问题。

items.example: A dogmatist fears the second question.
items.exampleCN: 教条主义者害怕第二个问题。

items.meaning: what is taught as a body
items.meaningCN: 作为整体被教导的内容
items.example: The doctrine shaped the school.
items.exampleCN: 这套学说塑造了这所学校。

items.meaning: a thing that shows or teaches
items.meaningCN: 用来显示或教导的东西
items.example: The document recorded the ruling.
items.exampleCN: 这份文件记录了裁决。

items.example: The docent explained the painting.
items.exampleCN: 讲解员解释了这幅画。

items.example: He was raised in an orthodox home.
items.exampleCN: 他在一个正统的家庭长大。
